Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Überbauung Freudenau
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A 55-unit housing estate in solid construction with single-leaf stonework, designed to Swiss Minergie energy standard.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Salgenreute Chapel
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A small alpine chapel built with timber construction and a limestone plinth, featuring a distinctive steeply rising wooden spatial fold that will weather to dark or silver-gray tones, with hand-sawn larch shingles, untreated fir interiors, and a design that frames views of the natural landscape through the apse.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Pfarrhaus Krumbach
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A rectory and multipurpose cultural building in timber construction with passive house energy performance, housing a parish hall, office, library, and music club rehearsal room.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Haus am Wiesenweg
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A single-family courtyard house with timber construction and an L-shaped footprint that prioritizes privacy, featuring a covered terrace, barrier-free ground-floor master suite, and upper-floor children's rooms.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Kindergarten Wiesenbach
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A kindergarten for 4 groups with refurbishment of a 1960s building into a mother-child-center, featuring concrete core walls and ceilings with preassembled highly insulated external elements and a heat pump energy system.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: House by the fens
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A residential and studio building in the Bregenzerwald region with a longitudinal pitched roof design, featuring a concrete core zone, highly insulated external elements, and extensive use of locally-sourced wood (spruce, fir, and elm) for structural parts, walls, and flooring, along with handmade brick clay tiles incorporating floor heating.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Susi Weigel Kindergarten
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A two-story kindergarten building with a square layout featuring concrete core walls and highly insulated preassembled external elements, with interiors of local fir wood and pine façade that references the surrounding landscape.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: House on Schopfacker
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A two-family house with a granny flat featuring solid timber construction with a concrete core, wood-paneling interiors, and a hipped roof that references traditional Appenzell regional architecture while meeting modern living standards.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Austrian Embassy
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A diplomatic residence for the Austrian Embassy featuring a single-story timber construction with a central courtyard dividing private living quarters from representative areas, constructed using hollow-core beams and prefabricated timber walls with native wood species interior and facade finishes.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Haus Fontanella
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A mountain house for a 6-member family featuring preassembled timber construction on a concrete and natural stone basement, with geothermal heating and a wood stove.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Islamic Cemetery
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A public Islamic cemetery in Vorarlberg featuring a clearly structured layout with concrete walls of varying heights framing grave plots, a prayer room with a mihrab facing Mecca, and a concrete farewell space, designed with sparse symbolic elements and integrated into the surrounding alluvial landscape.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Saunahaus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A sauna, massage, and therapy building featuring concrete core zones with highly insulated timber-element construction exterior, heated by a heat pump with groundwater well and solar hot water system.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Moorraum Krumbach
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A look-out and tracking structure built with traditional timber construction and a floor space of 80m² for the Municipality of Krumbach.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Schule und Saal Laterns
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A school and hall building in timber construction on a concrete and stone base, featuring geothermal heating and a wood stove, winning the Vorarlberger Holzbaupreis in 2013.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: House in the field
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A timber-constructed courtyard house with a pitched roof on a small corner plot, featuring an internalised courtyard with large sliding shutters framing Alpine views, wooden floors and paneling, and a low-energy standard with geothermal heating.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Kinderhaus Schruns
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A children's house built with timber construction and designed to passive house energy standards.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Kindergarten Dorf
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A kindergarten built with timber element construction from locally sourced wood, featuring interior spaces finished entirely in wood with references to regional architecture and passive house energy standards of 14 kWh/m²a.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Landesberufsschule
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: An extension and restoration of a vocational school featuring steel construction and geothermal energy systems integrated into the piled foundation.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Raumschicht Sütten
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: Integration of a small 100m² flat into an existing Vorderbregenzerwälder farmhouse using preassembled construction and pellet heating.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Metzgerstüble Mellau
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A small 80m² saloon building constructed in timber with low-energy performance standards and district heating.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Biomasse-HKW
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A biomass cogeneration plant with solid construction, timber roof and facade, designed to produce 20 million kWh of energy annually while avoiding approximately 8,000 tons of CO2 emissions.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Umweltinstitut
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A complete refurbishment of the Institutes for Umwelt und Lebensmittelsicherheit, an existing public building with a floor space of approximately 2,895 m².

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: EMA Haus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A 90m² private residence featuring preassembled construction with high-level prefabrication and a geothermal heat pump heating system.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: HD Haus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A house on a hill with timber element construction on a solid basement, heated by a heat pump with depth probe and wood stove.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Krone Hittisau
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A modification of a 180-year-old Bregenzerwälder tavern that retained its existing structure and district heating systems.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Haus Fohren
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A cottage for a retired couple and their guests built with modular, preassembled timber construction and heated by a wood stove and geothermal heat pump.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: AMA Haus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A family house in Bregenzerwald with timber construction, geothermal heating, and 150m² of floor space, winning distinction awards for its design.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: KR Haus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A massive timber house featuring a unique 'knitted' timber log-construction on a concrete base, with geothermal heat pump and wood stove for energy.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Dynamic Space Room
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A 180 m² showroom for fabric fixtures designed as a competition-winning project for Julius Blum GmbH.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: K Haus
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A village house with timber element construction on a concrete base, featuring a geothermal heat pump with depth probe for energy.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Friedhof Krumbach
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A cemetery with an urn-wall constructed from sawn and broken Bregenzerwälder limestone, spanning 1200 m².

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Haus Salgenreute
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: An extension of a 1970s holiday home featuring timber element construction on a partial concrete basement with a wood stove for heating.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Fußballclub Krumbach 2000
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A summer house for a local football club featuring preassembled construction on a deep foundation with no heating system.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: House Kaltschmieden
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A single-storey house with gable roof and minimized formal language, built with a core zone in light concrete and perimeter structure in white fir timber, incorporating materials and components salvaged from the demolished original farmhouse that previously occupied the site.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Village House Steinberg
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A multi-functional village community building constructed entirely of larch wood in timber construction with a biomass low-energy standard, designed to resemble a traditional Tyrolean farmhouse with a rough-sawn larch board façade and concrete plinth, housing a parish hall, coffee house, market place, and gymnasium.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Mosque and cultural centre
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A cultural center and mosque featuring a robust concrete building envelope with structural bronze elements around windows and minaret, soft interior finishes in white stained wood, and traditional elements including an interior courtyard and water features that blend regional, Islamic, and European architectural styles.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Golfclub Grand Resort
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A renewal of an existing golf clubhouse featuring a new structure with a widely projecting roof that unifies interior spaces, using exclusive materials and careful craftsmanship to create varied spatial moods with different heights and light qualities.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Bäumlequartier am See
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A residential estate of 130 apartments across approximately 10,300 square meters, composed of six twisted point-form building bodies that integrate existing structures and respond to neighboring development with a restrained architectural language.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Wolf Ski Hut Petersboda
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A ski lodge for 50 guests at 2000m elevation, featuring a prefabricated timber structure with sawed spruce slats exterior, rough-cut red fir interior, solid concrete core with open fireplace, and pellet heating system with waste heat utilization.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: Lodges at the Lake
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: Temporary simple lodges by Lake Constance featuring basic wood construction on point foundations with stove heating, each 40m² in floor space.

Bernardo Bader Architekten.name: House at the Stürcherwald
Bernardo Bader Architekten.description: A modern interpretation of traditional Walser long-house farming architecture, featuring prefabricated wood elements with rough-sawn larch exterior panels and a compact, elongated form positioned on a steeply sloping mountain plot at 1000 meters elevation.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Haus für Julia und Björn
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A single-family house that won multiple awards including the Houses of the Year 2015 and the Vorarlberg Timber Construction Prize 2015.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Haus mit Schauraum
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A combined residential and commercial building on a narrow, exposed lot along a municipal road, featuring a showroom and office on the north facade with private residential spaces organized across two floors to the south.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Panoramarestaurant Seilbahn Bezau
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A mountain restaurant designed to conform to the existing topography, with the building volume nestled against the hillside and an inset external staircase leading to a roof terrace.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Haus für Gudrun
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A single-family house organized around a central core containing utilities and bathrooms, featuring a large living space, two small bedrooms, white spruce wood walls with integrated deep-set windows and built-in elements, and a central dark concrete core contrasting with the surrounding light wood.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Österreichische Botschaft in Zagreb
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A single-story embassy building featuring equally-ranked functions organized around a central atrium that enhances all adjacent spaces with views and open areas.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Seedomaine Lochau
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A mixed-use residential development with 200 apartments, shops, and offices on a 23,000 m² site, designed to sensitively integrate building forms into the landscape while creating private and semi-public spaces with views of the lake.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Kindergarten Blattacker
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A kindergarten building featuring separate additive units with courtyards and glass fronts allowing visual transparency through the structure, designed with a clean spatial and structural system.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Bergkapelle Wirmboden
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A public chapel that won awards for its color, structure, and surface treatment design.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Villa D
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A villa designed by Architekten Innauer Matt in collaboration with Bernardo Bader Architekten, which won third prize in a 2015 competition.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Georunde Rindberg
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A landscape and educational walking trail that documents a 1999 landslide disaster in the Rindberg area, with stations that make the forces of nature visible and convey knowledge about how the village residents coped with the event.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Stadtbücherei Dornbirn
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A public library designed with a simple flexible structural logic and a focused classical central space theme to create an open knowledge and idea space characterized by an atmosphere of great relaxation.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Mittlere 81
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A revitalization project in Bezau, Austria completed in 2016.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Townhouse Pia
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A townhouse study project designed by Architekten Innauer Matt with Simon Moosbrugger as project lead.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Patscherkofelbahn
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A cable car station complex comprising valley, middle, and mountain stations designed as cohesive architectural volumes featuring functional vertical and horizontal elements, massive bodies for cable car infrastructure, and expansive glazing to frame the surrounding mountain landscape.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Strubobuob Gartenwerkstatt
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A commercial extension building for a garden shop that combines two previously separate business locations, featuring a covered entrance with display areas, sales space across two floors, and distinctive side gables that reference the surrounding architecture.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Kindergarten am Engelbach
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A compact, two-story kindergarten building designed to create a distinctive world for children with a residential character, combining the site's potential with modern pedagogical requirements through openness to interior and exterior spaces.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: KUNSTRAUM KASSEL
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A new exhibition hall for the Kassel University of Art, designed by Architekten Innauer Matt as the winner of a design competition.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Berghaus Eller
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A three-story residential house designed with economic restraint, featuring a whole-house tiled stove for energy efficiency, locally-sourced timber materials, and a central living area with a tile stove as the family's social heart.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Bücklepark
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A mixed-use urban quarter development on a former Siemens site comprising residential, commercial, and service spaces integrated with public areas and neighboring districts across approximately 70,000 square meters.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Deutsch-Deutsches Museum
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A competition-winning museum design featuring an abstract, wall-like structure that deliberately confronts the natural topography of the hillside, referencing the arbitrary nature of border demarcations.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Strandbad Lochau
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A single-story public beach bathhouse with a wide protective roof and wooden post-and-beam structure that mediates between a lake, existing pier, and new stream outlet.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Kinderhaus Kreuzfeld
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A kindergarten and early childhood care facility designed as an identity-forming new center for sustainable residential development in a green inner space.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Firmenzentrale Jägerbau
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A corporate headquarters building for the Jäger Group that integrates surrounding urban areas with clearly defined city edges and flexible, open interior structures.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: LERNHAUS BEZAU
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A combined primary school and kindergarten building for children aged 4 to 10, designed as an integrated educational facility that serves as an urban centerpiece for the village of Bezau.

Innauer Matt Architekten.name: Kraftwerk Dürrenbach
Innauer Matt Architekten.description: A small hydroelectric power plant (Kleinwasserkraftanlage) designed for Illwerke VKW.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Showroom AD
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A restoration of an early 20th-century neoclassical villa combined with a new two-level concrete showroom extension featuring large glazed surfaces and flexible exhibition spaces, with materials including concrete and plastered surfaces positioned on the villa's eastern grounds.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa SSG
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A three-volume residential compound in the Treviso countryside featuring a prominent roof design, fluid interior spaces with large glazed openings, and varying interior heights that frame views across the landscape.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: IPES SCENA
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A compact multi-level building with three above-ground floors arranged over sloped terrain, featuring glass mosaic-clad façades inspired by local stone terracing and designed with sustainable materials and strong attention to environmental criteria.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Asiago Retirement Home
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A competition-winning redevelopment of a nursing home and former barracks complex featuring reorganized volumes, unified public and semi-public spaces, service blocks on each floor, and residential rooms designed as monastic cells with integrated furnishings and views toward the mountain landscape.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: CASA SAN MARTINO
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A renovation of a 1970s apartment that combines reclaimed larch wood for floors, walls, and furniture with a concrete, iron, and wood fireplace, creating a contemporary space with views of the pale di San Martino mountains.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Fire Station
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A fire station competition project featuring a two-story building on a triangular lot with technical/storage areas on the lower floor, personnel and administrative spaces above, and a detached training tower serving as the project's distinctive architectural element.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Middle School Cavaion Veronese
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A new middle school and gym designed as a single multifunctional building that integrates with the landscape through careful attention to existing trees, open partitionable spaces, and a combination of green and mineral surfaces, with innovative teaching spaces that blur the boundaries between interior classrooms and exterior learning areas.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Kindergarden Longarone
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A kindergarten building located on the historic Murazzi containment system, designed with a timber structure and cladding featuring geometric decorations inspired by trees, incorporating flexible modular spaces and multiple outdoor learning areas connected to the surrounding landscape.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: CASA DLS
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A two-level house with underground level designed around a central cast-in-place concrete wall that organizes spaces, features simple lines and authentic materials, with the ground floor containing living areas and kitchen opening to a garden, and upper level with three bedrooms.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Scuola Elementare Magliaso
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A contemporary elementary school and gym building whose volume aligns with existing structures and uses pigmentation to blend with the surrounding hill landscape, accompanied by landscaping including rows of trees and a communal lawn space.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa Roveri
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A restored terraced house originally dating from the early 1800s in Treviso's Fiera district, formerly part of a rural villa complex, featuring original wooden staircases and floors, with a narrow garden and cautious interventions that preserved historical elements while creating more intimate bedroom spaces.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa BC
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A restored early 1900s two-storey house with attic (240 sqm) featuring a converted garage roof terrace and private courtyard, with exposed iron structure, microcement and oak wood floors, and black iron architectural elements.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Europan 14
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A mixed-use urban development competition project featuring commercial, productive, and residential spaces organized vertically around three colored towers (Black, Red, and Yellow) with roof gardens, cycling routes, and connections to an adjacent school.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa VP
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A 60-square-meter apartment in historic Treviso's city center featuring exposed wooden beams and original bricks, light grey resin flooring, custom iron windows and kitchen elements, and vintage furnishings arranged to accommodate the owner's passion for reading and vintage objects.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Nobrowhood
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: An exhibition design featuring modular tables made of natural fir wood with matte black surfaces, organized to create an itinerary through works by five illustrators from the Nobrow publishing company.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: The Play Park
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A competition-winning skate park in Ballyfermot that integrates existing trees and natural topography through dug-in concrete bowls of varying heights, designed with colored concrete to create three skill-level areas while maintaining views from the adjacent street.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa 2x1
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A merged two-unit residence featuring an open ground floor with kitchen, dining room, and living room, and an upper floor with bedrooms, guest room, and studio, unified by clear large-tile flooring that creates brightness and spatial continuity.

Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.name: Casa Fiera
Galeotti Rizzato Architetti.description: A restored historic house in Treviso's Porto di Fiera district with a modern wooden-clad addition, featuring recovered original roof beams and new openings framing views of the adjacent Sant'Ambrogio church.

Loader Monteith.name: Ceangal House
Loader Monteith.description: A new five-bedroom courtyard house on a working farm featuring three pitched gables, reclaimed sandstone cladding and over 4000 reclaimed bricks from demolished steading buildings, with sinusoidal red agricultural-style cladding and extensive glazing connecting interior spaces to the private courtyard.

Loader Monteith.name: The Maker's House
Loader Monteith.description: A reunified stone villa in a conservation area with a new concrete extension featuring a roof light, insulation, and on-site heat pump, designed to serve as both family home and working studio.

Loader Monteith.name: The Carpenter's House
Loader Monteith.description: A B-listed former carpenter's house with parged red sandstone rubble walls, ballachulish slate and red pantile roof, and crow-step gables, refurbished and extended with a standing seam metal roof extension featuring large-format glazing to connect living spaces to the walled garden.

Loader Monteith.name: Strone of Glenbanchor
Loader Monteith.description: A refurbished and extended former crofter's cottage featuring original rubble stone walls and slate roof combined with timber-clad extensions, designed as a light-filled mountain retreat with views toward the Cairngorms.

Loader Monteith.name: The Origami House
Loader Monteith.description: An extension and internal reconfiguration of a Scottish cottage in a conservation village, featuring a 15 square metre addition with a folded pitched roof, Douglas fir window seat, exposed timber structure, and neutral natural materials including soft white walls and light microcement flooring.

Loader Monteith.name: The Rower's House
Loader Monteith.description: A complete renovation of a London home featuring an open-plan kitchen, dining and living room with exposed limed timber roof structure, large triple-glazed windows, a central rooflight, underfloor heating, photovoltaic panels, and a garden connection.

Loader Monteith.name: The Collector's Home
Loader Monteith.description: Internal reconfiguration of a ground floor flat in a subdivided Georgian villa, relocating the kitchen to the center of the home and creating a bright day room with salvaged beech flooring, Bert and May tiles, and a concrete worktop by Billy Teasdale.

Loader Monteith.name: The Cook's House
Loader Monteith.description: A reorganized Victorian terrace house featuring a bright, centrally-positioned U-shaped kitchen with muted blue palette and oak joinery, custom oak banquette seating in the dining area, and large glazed doors connecting the interior to the rear garden.

Loader Monteith.name: The Shieling
Loader Monteith.description: A historic cottage renovation and extension in a conservation area featuring a folding roof with glass clerestory, birch ply interiors, slate flooring, and sliding glazing to frame views of the Campsie Fells.

Loader Monteith.name: Kingsborough Gardens
Loader Monteith.description: An extension and internal reconfiguration of a B-listed townhouse in Glasgow's conservation area, featuring a modern addition in large format wet cast concrete and weathering steel that connects the kitchen and living spaces to the back garden, with new staircases, underfloor heating, and improved insulation.

Loader Monteith.name: Of the Hill
Loader Monteith.description: A new build house on a hillside overlooking the Scottish coastline, made of prevailing landscape materials with a stone wall emerging from the hillside that forms an enclosed garden.

Loader Monteith.name: Gable House
Loader Monteith.description: A new build family home in rural Perthshire designed to reference historic gable forms on the site, featuring open living spaces with rural views, timber throughout, and Passivhaus standards.

Loader Monteith.name: The Equine House
Loader Monteith.description: A 155 square metre family home on a subdivided dairy farm featuring a striking red aluminium-framed window seat, black-stained larch cladding, white render, triple glazing, and sustainable systems including an air source heat pump and recycled aluminium roof.

Loader Monteith.name: Fan House
Loader Monteith.description: A transformed 1930s semi-detached four-bedroom house featuring a slanting wraparound extension with Douglas fir beams, large windows, oak veneer cabinetry, and a monolithic grey exterior that blends with the local landscape.

Loader Monteith.name: Pitch House
Loader Monteith.description: A new family home built on a hillside in rural Perthshire, formed from former agricultural sheds with an undulating roof pitch and constructed with highly insulated SIPs panels, preserving views across a courtyard to the landscape.

Loader Monteith.name: Cairnconon Byre
Loader Monteith.description: A contemporary single-family home built on the East Coast of Scotland that reuses reclaimed stone from an existing ruinous byre, featuring an L-shaped plan with polished concrete floors, floor-to-ceiling windows, and a sinusoidal metal roof inspired by local agricultural buildings.

Loader Monteith.name: Old Red House
Loader Monteith.description: A retrofitted terraced house stripped to brickwork and rebuilt with Passivhaus principles, featuring a double-sided fireplace, bespoke birch plywood kitchen, high-performance glazing, green roof, and air source heat pump to achieve a low-energy, gas-free home.

Loader Monteith.name: Dulnain House
Loader Monteith.description: A contemporary home composed of two linked volumes—one in recycled granite stone and one in charred timber—designed to honor the site's history while incorporating passive systems and responding to modern climate realities.

Herbst Architects.name: Omata Beach House
Herbst Architects.description: A beachside residential house designed by Herbst Architects that won multiple NZIA architecture awards in 2023 for housing design.

Herbst Architects.name: Onetangi Cliff house
Herbst Architects.description: A beach house carved into the base of a cliff on Waiheke Island, recognized as Coastal Home of the Year 2025.

Herbst Architects.name: Omata Hill House - Alterations
Herbst Architects.description: An alteration project on a residential house in Omata, which won a New Zealand architecture award for housing in 2023.

Herbst Architects.name: Dune House
Herbst Architects.description: A seaside residential project by Herbst Architects that won a 2022 HERE award for interior architecture, featuring collaboration with structural engineering, landscaping, and custom furniture design.

Herbst Architects.name: Lantern House Waiheke
Herbst Architects.description: A primary residence on a steep coastal slope featuring a two-level design with living spaces on the lower level stretched along the land contour and guest accommodation on the upper level, articulated by a continuous window seat and sheltered courtyard.

Herbst Architects.name: Kawakawa House Piha
Herbst Architects.description: A year-round beach house designed to maximize ocean views and natural light on a challenging sun-limited site, featuring an upper-level living area with continuous clerestory windows, open central courtyard, and covered deck overlooking Pohutukawa trees and mountains.

Herbst Architects.name: Bethells Bach
Herbst Architects.location: Te Henga (Bethells), 30km North-West of Auckland City
Herbst Architects.description: A two-bedroom bach overlooking a hillside, clad in vertical cedar boards that wrap inside, featuring a covered deck with fireplace, semi-enclosed rear terrace, timber batten screens, and a central courtyard with volcanic rocks.

Herbst Architects.name: K Valley House
Herbst Architects.description: A retreat for filmmakers on 20 hectares of farmland, clad in a rainscreen of rusted corrugated iron sheets and constructed largely from recycled materials and fittings, with a singular geometric form positioned straddling the ridgeline.

Herbst Architects.name: Muriwai House
Herbst Architects.description: A family dwelling sited within an existing copse of nikau palms on the West Coast.

Herbst Architects.name: Mission Bay Pavilion restaurant
Herbst Architects.description: A new purpose-built restaurant designed to complement the renovation of existing Melanesian Mission Heritage buildings, with interiors by Herbst Architects in conjunction with Katie Lockhart Studio.

Herbst Architects.name: Bay of Islands House
Herbst Architects.description: A house overlooking the Bay of Islands designed by Herbst Architects.

Herbst Architects.name: Omaha Beach House
Herbst Architects.description: A beach house located at Omaha, designed by Herbst Architects.

Herbst Architects.name: Bramasole House
Herbst Architects.description: A residential house on a former market garden and vineyard site in Waimauku, featuring three box-form elements clad in weathered timber with a central living pavilion, gabion basket walls dividing the site, and elevated on a blockwork plinth.

Herbst Architects.name: Castle Rock Beach House
Herbst Architects.description: A beach house featuring blunt, uncompromising materials designed to age naturally, with open spaces that invite sand and weathering as part of its distinctive sense of place.

Herbst Architects.name: Clevedon Estate - Additions
Herbst Architects.description: Two pavilion-like additions to an existing house: a pool pavilion with elegant proportions and refined materials, and a garage/office building with a central courtyard featuring a solitary tree reaching through a roof opening.

Herbst Architects.name: Wetland Folly
Herbst Architects.description: A small cooking, dining and relaxing pavilion with a simple structural frame over-clad with awnings, screens and translucent sheet, designed as a holiday retreat structure celebrating bach lifestyle.

Herbst Architects.name: Te Modular
Herbst Architects.description: A small bach (holiday shelter) design of 87m2 developed as a repeatable model that distills essential elements for a magical holiday home while controlling costs and size, built traditionally by local builders with only minor site modifications.

Herbst Architects.name: Under Pohutukawa
Herbst Architects.description: A beach house designed as a sympathetically placed pavilion that nestles among pohutukawa trees, featuring an opened-up summer configuration and executed with perfectionist precision to harmonize structure with its natural setting.

Herbst Architects.name: Logan Vault
Herbst Architects.description: A major renovation to a grand old villa that transforms the interior through a dialogue between preserved and newly invented elements.

Herbst Architects.name: Kaipara Pavilion
Herbst Architects.description: A pavilion and swimming pool enclosure overlooking Kaipara harbour featuring a post-and-beam structure in rough-cut pine with a pitched roof, cedar slat screens, integrated kitchen facilities, steel wok barbecue, and a solar panel system for pool heating and circulation.

Herbst Architects.name: Bark House
Herbst Architects.description: A family home on a heavily wooded site with boldly executed forms using a limited palette of natural materials, designed to take advantage of limited vistas while bringing an urban edge to a rural setting.

Herbst Architects.name: Paremoremo House
Herbst Architects.description: A house on an undulating lifestyle block organized around a central courtyard bounded by cedar-shuttered pavilions on three sides, with views toward open landscape on the fourth side.

Herbst Architects.name: Inside out Bach
Herbst Architects.description: A summer holiday house with a linear plan transformed into individual spaces by a covered outdoor deck, sun court, and seating areas, featuring block piers, double timber posts, delicate trusses, and translucent walls that enclose private terraces.

Herbst Architects.name: Kaitoke Bach
Herbst Architects.description: A timber and glass retreat organized with a simple orthogonal plan, featuring layered screens, shady verandahs, and warm interior finishes contrasting with bleached natural exterior materials of timber and stone.

Herbst Architects.name: Oruawharo Bay Bach
Herbst Architects.description: A bach featuring a restrained palette of raw materials including a solid gabion wall, double columns, and timber boxes with generous openings, timber batten cladding, and rough gabion walls that create changing shadow play throughout the day.

Herbst Architects.name: Hammerhead House
Herbst Architects.description: A seaside bach featuring a crisp wooden box on a concrete block base, with living areas on the first floor connected to a terrace by exterior stair, bedrooms in the concrete base, and an animated exterior envelope created by robust timber detailing and movable sunscreen devices.

Herbst Architects.name: Wonderview House
Herbst Architects.description: A hybrid house/bach designed for a young couple featuring a rectilinear spiral block wall foundation anchoring the building into steep landscape, with a lightweight one-bedroom bach cantilevering over the plinth, oriented toward southern views with a north-facing roof opening for sunlight.

Herbst Architects.name: Aotea Bach
Herbst Architects.description: A pavilion-style bach on Great Barrier Island with two open sides allowing the landscape to flow through, featuring a south terrace on a shallow slope and a north deck overlooking an olive grove.

Herbst Architects.name: Island Bach
Herbst Architects.description: A bach on Great Barrier Island featuring a tower and pavilion sheathed in weathered timber planks with sliding panels that blur interior and exterior distinctions, combining bach tradition with modernist formal sensibility.

Herbst Architects.name: Herbst Bach
Herbst Architects.description: An experimental minimal bach featuring a room, veranda, and essential ablution facilities with lockable cupboards and sliding screens for security and weathering protection.

Patterson Associates.name: Pouaka Waikura Rust Sheds
Patterson Associates.description: A rural residential compound of four robust rectilinear pavilions clad in off-form concrete, Corten steel, and blackened steel joinery, designed for wine-making and car restoration on a 1.8-hectare terraced site overlooking the Shotover River.

Patterson Associates.name: Royal Auckland and Grange Golf Club
Fendalton House
Patterson Associates.description: A two-level contemporary home with a white triple-gabled roof built on the footprint of a 1910 house destroyed in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, featuring a central entry hallway with an eight-metre ceiling, full-height garden openings, a sculptural spiral staircase, and a passenger lift, designed to honor the spatial relationships of the original home while celebrating the owners' art collection and antique furniture.

Patterson Associates.name: Geyser
Patterson Associates.description: A multi-tenanted, mixed-use commercial development featuring five sub-buildings arranged around atriums and courtyards, wrapped in dynamic semi-reflective white twin-walled façades, and New Zealand's first 6-star Green Star certified building.

Patterson Associates.name: Maungakawa
Patterson Associates.description: A radially symmetrical family home clad in custom orange plantation-grown renewable timber with on-site water harvesting and wastewater treatment, designed to echo the calm of a Gordon Walters painting and situated in a forest clearing overlooking the Waikato farmlands.

Patterson Associates.name: Olive Grove
Patterson Associates.description: A residential home surrounded by an existing olive grove on west-facing slopes, featuring a two-way spanning cantilevered timber roof that shelters a multi-purpose room, changing rooms, and north-facing terrace overlooking a swimming pool and tennis court.

Patterson Associates.name: Stratis
Patterson Associates.description: A six-storey apartment building with 65 units wrapped around a central marina, designed as a stack of containers with white GRC, concrete, and glass, referencing the site's former container terminal history.

Patterson Associates.name: Anvil
Patterson Associates.description: A medium-sized mixed-use commercial building on a prominent corner featuring flexible boutique tenancies, an elevated circulation courtyard, and a distinctive spiral car parking ramp veiled in fritted glass.

Patterson Associates.name: Axis
Patterson Associates.description: A 4000m2 mixed-use retrofit and conversion of Auckland's historic Nestle Chocolate factory featuring commercial offices, showrooms, residential apartments, restaurants and cafes, organized around a large internal courtyard.

Patterson Associates.name: D72
Patterson Associates.description: A mixed-use commercial conversion featuring a woven aluminium façade to filter sunlight, with 5400m² of commercial space organized around a spiral-shaped central courtyard.

Patterson Associates.name: Frankfurt Book Fair
Patterson Associates.description: The New Zealand Guest of Honour Pavilion featured a model of New Zealand as a floating island under a starry sky, with six 5-metre high sub-pavilions containing intimate libraries and suspended books as chandeliers, accompanied by an audio-visual show referencing how literature speaks to audiences.

Patterson Associates.name: Site 3
Patterson Associates.description: A mixed-use commercial development of 6000m2 featuring new buildings with exposed steel frames and distinctive window shutters inserted around a historic 1883 stables building with category 1 heritage listing.

Patterson Associates.name: Swan Lake
Patterson Associates.description: A 705m2 private residence constructed in rusted core 10 steel, skim rendered brickwork, and aluminium pivoting joinery, centered around a courtyard with an artificial infinity-edged reflection lake and sculptural hillocks framing views of Coronet Peak and the Wakatipu landscape.

Patterson Associates.name: Annandale Homestead
Patterson Associates.description: A restored 1884 historic hotel building adapted for luxury use, featuring traditional timber and daub construction with contemporary earthquake strengthening and modern services incorporated sensitively.

Patterson Associates.name: Wanaka Lodge
Patterson Associates.description: A sun-oriented residential lodge crafted in local schist stone with two large pavilions enclosing a private courtyard, designed to reference a Southern Italian masseria while reflecting the surrounding Southern Alps landscape.

Patterson Associates.name: Cumulus
Patterson Associates.description: A small mixed-use commercial building featuring glass reinforced concrete panelling, three levels of parking, and eight office tenancies arranged around a sky courtyard with elevator access to a rooftop garden.

Patterson Associates.name: Black Peak / Mount Burke
Patterson Associates.description: A light timber-framed house on the shore of Lake Wanaka with charred larch cladding and a local stone plinth, designed as two pavilions (main home and guest house) aligned to mountain views, with the kitchen as a central hub for both intimate and extended family living.

Patterson Associates.name: Ravenscar House Museum
Patterson Associates.description: A purpose-built house museum featuring four chambers arranged around a central courtyard, constructed from pre-cast concrete made with crushed bricks from the original destroyed home and rubble from other city buildings.

Patterson Associates.name: Christchurch Botanic Garden Centre
Patterson Associates.description: A public botanic garden centre designed as a contemporary greenhouse with a sawtooth roof, featuring airy thresholds with public spaces including a shop and café, alongside educational and research facilities, with sculptural ceiling panels that filter light like woodland shade.

Patterson Associates.name: Le Calligramme Memorial
Patterson Associates.description: A public memorial sculpture designed for the French government, constructed from French limestone with polished metal letters and incorporating soft landscaping, a honed plinth, and a vertical sculpture with integrated audio and lighting components.

Patterson Associates.name: Len Lye Centre
Patterson Associates.description: A public art gallery and cultural center featuring curved stainless steel and concrete construction with gallery spaces, education studios, a cinema, and a dedicated motor room for kinetic sculptures, incorporating a light-reflecting facade and sustainable energy systems.

Patterson Associates.name: Kinloch Lodge
Patterson Associates.description: A clubhouse and lodge facility for a Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course, constructed of bagged stone on blockwork with turret-like chimneys, featuring an internal courtyard, deep window bays, and accompanying duplex units clad in black stained cedar.

Patterson Associates.name: Local Rock House
Patterson Associates.description: A New Zealand coastal residence for an expatriate family on a steep escarpment, featuring a prominent rock mass structure that creates living areas nestled into the landscape with a northern terrace and western courtyard, using local materials to integrate with its setting above a pohutukawa-fringed beach.

Patterson Associates.name: Seascape Retreat
Patterson Associates.description: A beachside cottage built into a rock escarpment using locally quarried rock, in-situ concrete floors, and an earth turfed roof, with macrocarpa wood interior lining and earthquake-resistant glazing, designed as a self-sustainable honeymoon retreat.

Patterson Associates.name: Scrubby Bay House
Patterson Associates.description: A robust farmhouse set on a remote coastal sheep and cattle station, featuring a vernacular form with macrocarpa timber interior, a central stone fireplace built from quarried station rock, and custom-designed steel fittings and furnishings.

Patterson Associates.name: Pines House
Patterson Associates.description: A family bach composed of zinc-clad pavilions arranged around pine trees, featuring a long front deck with views, corrugated zinc cladding extending into the interior, and a sloping sylvan courtyard, with the beach in front.

Patterson Associates.name: The Michael Hill Golf Clubhouse
Patterson Associates.description: A golf clubhouse with a divot-like roof, golf ball claddings, and an integral truss system supporting a green roof planted in native tussock, designed to integrate into the alpine landscape with less than a third of its volume above ground.

Patterson Associates.name: Waiheke House
Patterson Associates.description: A residential pavilion on a sloped site with a sculptural timber-clad roof suspended above extensively glazed living and sleeping areas, an embedded in situ concrete base containing services, and a geometrically-matched swimming pool integrated into the landscape.

Patterson Associates.name: Aesop
Patterson Associates.description: A commercial Aesop store designed to feel like an intimate neighborhood space, featuring native timber boarding and weathered galvanised steel materials reminiscent of traditional New Zealand bach architecture and colonial washrooms.

Patterson Associates.name: Boat Shed Bay
Patterson Associates.description: A secluded holiday home comprising three connected pavilions arranged around a north-facing courtyard, featuring roof forms and board and batten cladding that echo historic boatsheds nearby.

Patterson Associates.name: Naisoso Island
Patterson Associates.description: A new tropical home built with local trade block, in-situ plastered concrete, and imported aluminium joinery with security fins that function as storm shutters and sun shades, featuring a coral stone wall and white interior on cool concrete floors.

Patterson Associates.name: Country House in the City
Patterson Associates.description: A residential home featuring a steel frame structure with alternating windows and glass-reinforced concrete panels inspired by late 1960s Italian modernism, organized around a central farmhouse kitchen and working garden room surrounded by greenery.

Patterson Associates.name: Mai Mai
Patterson Associates.description: A home for a couple featuring white fibreglass exterior walls with a feathery motif referencing traditional Māori cloaks, and interior spaces including a glass-surrounded sitting room, leather-lined den, and interior courtyard with city views.

Patterson Associates.name: Parihoa
Patterson Associates.description: A contemporary rural house positioned on a wind-swept coastal hill with black stained exterior boards and timber interiors, designed as a fortress-like structure that wraps around a protected circulation courtyard while preserving the surrounding landscape.

Welsh + Major.name: Seagrass House
Welsh + Major.description: A robust beachfront house clad in corbelled brickwork that reflects the colors and textures of the surrounding rocky headland, designed to withstand bushfire risk while featuring spaces suspended in trees overlooking the beach.

Welsh + Major.name: Goodman Multi Story Industrial
Welsh + Major.description: A multi-level industrial warehouse and distribution complex featuring 3 levels of warehousing, a 7-storey office building, café, conferencing facilities, rooftop gardens, and wellness spaces powered by a 2MW photovoltaic array.

Welsh + Major.name: Annandale House
Welsh + Major.description: A contemporary family home set behind an existing weatherboard cottage, featuring interlocking brick masonry volumes arranged like telescope tubes to maximize light, air, and open space for a busy family of four.

Welsh + Major.name: The Sanctuary
Welsh + Major.description: A sheltered public gathering space designed as part of a larger cemetery upgrade project that includes landscape rejuvenation, walking tracks, parking areas, a public internment vault, and columbarium walls.

Welsh + Major.name: Wentworth Falls Lake Amenities
Welsh + Major.description: A public amenities building featuring brickwork patterned after the Blue Mountains Water Skink, with public toilet facilities, sheltered gathering space, and integrated public artwork by local artist Chris Tobin.

Welsh + Major.name: Albert Street
Welsh + Major.description: A house featuring a precast concrete culvert creating street presence, with sequences of external and internal spaces using timber and off-form concrete in their natural state, and a floating roof with three-sided clerestory for natural light and seasonal views.

Welsh + Major.name: Twin Set
Welsh + Major.description: A semi-detached house expanded into its twin to accommodate a large family, reoriented around a central garden courtyard with concrete cassettes and a new pavilion framing the courtyard and living spaces.

Welsh + Major.name: Cohen Park
Welsh + Major.description: A public amenities building constructed with robust masonry inspired by a remnant warehouse brick wall, incorporating timber, fibre cement and steel details to create filtered natural light and ventilation.

Welsh + Major.name: Hordern Street
Welsh + Major.description: An alteration to an inner-city house featuring a steel-framed addition clad with pre-cast concrete panel off-cuts, with a pitched roof designed to capture light while maintaining privacy and respecting the adjacent sandstone stable wall and cottage.

Welsh + Major.name: The Garden Project
Welsh + Major.description: A renovation of a late-Victorian home featuring an in-situ concrete garden room with timber and steel elements that blur boundaries between indoor and outdoor spaces, creating flexible accommodation with a central garden focus.

Welsh + Major.name: Light House
Welsh + Major.description: A significant alteration to a semi-detached house featuring two new double-height volumes clad in waterstruck bricks with folded ground planes and a northern courtyard with plunge pool.

Welsh + Major.name: Leura Loo
Welsh + Major.description: A public toilet facility featuring a glass mosaic mural inspired by the seasonal colours of the local gardens.

Welsh + Major.name: House 6
Welsh + Major.description: A terrace house renovation that adds 6 square metres of space to the rear through selective replacement of elements, creating flexible spaces that respond to occupants' needs.

Welsh + Major.name: Venus Bay House
Welsh + Major.description: A modest, cost-effective beach house built from corrugated metal, fibre cement sheet, plywood and galvanised steel, featuring sustainable systems including photovoltaic cells, solar hot water, rainwater tanks and on-site blackwater treatment.

Welsh + Major.name: Bathurst Animal Rehoming Centre
Welsh + Major.description: A public animal rehoming facility featuring animal enclosures, an adoption pavilion, companion animal training facility, and educational workshop spaces with interconnecting walkways.

Welsh + Major.name: 66 Wentworth
Welsh + Major.description: A public and commercial interior revitalization of a 1980s building featuring reinvigorated stone bas-relief artwork with new lighting and colorful reflection pieces across multiple foyer spaces.

Welsh + Major.name: Jacksons on George
Welsh + Major.description: A hospitality venue created by transforming a brutalist Port Jackson Tavern building with retractable copper roof elements, operable glass facade panels, projecting balconies, and rooftop terraces to activate a public plaza on George Street.

Welsh + Major.name: Endeavour Tap Rooms
Welsh + Major.description: A 1880s former hotel building adapted into a casual drinking and dining venue featuring vaulted arches over the main bar, green marble tables, and multiple rooms designed to reflect different characters of beer ranges.

Welsh + Major.name: Comedor
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use of a historic factory transformed into a restaurant and bar featuring ultramarine and red oxide painted surfaces, hand-crafted Japanese tiles, timber banquette seating, and a 16-metre stone and tile kitchen bar.

Welsh + Major.name: Argyle Well
Welsh + Major.location: Coodye / Millers Point, Gadigal Land, NSW
Welsh + Major.description: A heritage terrace house built in the 1840s and first renovated in the 1890s, restored to its original single-dwelling arrangement with contemporary interventions including a new concrete pavilion connected via a sandstone basement link that features a water feature housed in the remnants of an original colonial well.

Welsh + Major.name: The Imperial
Welsh + Major.description: A heritage-listed hotel building on a clifftop site featuring restored balconies and rejuvenated internal spaces with 2 new dining rooms offering sweeping coastal views.

Welsh + Major.name: The Hat Factory
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use project converting a historic hat factory into 2 dwellings with permeable glass and masonry spaces that balance heritage memory with flexible urban living.

Welsh + Major.name: Kiandra Courthouse + Chalet
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use of heritage buildings designed for accommodation, an interpretive resource centre and café in a remote location, featuring robust design with ESD principles including electricity co-generation, black water treatment, and passive solar design.

Welsh + Major.name: The Fenwick
Welsh + Major.description: A historic 1880s tugboat store restored and adapted into a public cafe and gallery space, featuring a dramatic new stair and concealed commercial kitchen while respecting the original building's heritage significance.

Welsh + Major.name: Tayim Restaurant + Bar
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use restaurant and bar inserted into the basement of an 1880s warehouse building, featuring a floating canopy and internally revealing original sandstone walls contrasted with polished plaster and bead blasted stainless steel elements.

Welsh + Major.name: A House With Tiles On It
Cascades Female Factory
Welsh + Major.description: A History and Interpretation Centre for the Cascades Female Factory World Heritage site featuring a reflective building skin overlaid with historic colonial landscape paintings that reflect the enclosing sandstone yard walls to merge past and present.

Welsh + Major.name: The Mercantile Hotel
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use and heritage project transforming an iconic hotel in The Rocks with new bars, a main kitchen, bistro, rooftop function areas, and revitalized short stay accommodation and public bar.

Welsh + Major.name: Park Masterplans
Welsh + Major.description: Master plans for eight priority parks within the Inner West LGA involving upgrade, maintenance, and facility distribution to create inviting and safe recreational spaces responding to community consultation and demographic needs.

Welsh + Major.name: Former Rocks Police Station
Welsh + Major.year: 1880s (original design); adaptive reuse project date not specified
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive reuse of a Palladian city gate police station from the 1880s, converted into a restaurant/cafe with new dining rooms, commercial kitchen, and refined detailing in brass, copper, glass, and black painted steel.

Welsh + Major.name: Darling Lane
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive reuse project that added rooms above an existing garage using a fenestrated laneway facade with window proportions derived from the original building's openings.

Welsh + Major.name: Lindfield Village Green
Welsh + Major.description: A public and commercial civic centre project that transformed a car park into a vibrant hub featuring underground carparking, open green play areas, endemic planting, retail spaces, markets, and public amenities.

Welsh + Major.name: Fitzroy Terrace
Welsh + Major.description: A state heritage listed Georgian terrace from circa 1845 in Sydney that underwent adaptive re-use alterations involving careful removal and reuse of materials, with experimentation in existing and recycled elements to create rich variation in surface form, colour and texture.

Welsh + Major.name: AS Tanner
Welsh + Major.description: A multi-purpose pavilion built primarily for archery with a generous verandah, toilet amenities, and groundskeepers rooms, located on the edge of Scarborough Ponds creek within the Rockdale wetlands corridor.

Welsh + Major.name: Pyrmont Community Centre
Welsh + Major.description: An adaptive re-use of the heritage-listed Pyrmont Public School that introduces new built form including an entry, gym, and music/performance space alongside multi-use community rooms, library link, reading spaces, and childcare facilities.

Welsh + Major.name: Greybox
Welsh + Major.description: A courtyard house designed for outdoor living, featuring a 3-sided verandah wrapping around a central courtyard with separate rooms, inspired by homestead, beachside motel, tractor shed, and abbey typologies.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Rockbound
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential house that emerges from rocky terrain with primary living spaces parallel to the water, featuring naturally weathering materials and panoramic views toward Peggy's Cove Lighthouse.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Prime Seafood Palace
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A light-filled wood cathedral restaurant in West Queen West designed with white maple and brass materials to create a timeless, trend-free space for Canadian chef Matty Matheson's cuisine.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: OG House
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential project in Halifax's North End featuring a primary residence for the architect above a ground-floor community studio dedicated to neighborhood projects including housing for the homeless and public amenities.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: White Rock
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A 1,500 sqft residential house perched above a steep rocky incline overlooking the Gaspereau River Valley, completed in summer 2023.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Fisher & Paykel Toronto Experience Centre
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: An adaptive reuse experience centre housed in the Boiler House of the former Toronto Carpet Manufacturing Company, merging historical preservation with modern design to showcase Fisher & Paykel appliances.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Jib House
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential house on a triangular coastal lot in Chester Village with south-facing views overlooking the Chester basin and nearby islands.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Fyren
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential beacon set atop a high sea-side plateau in the Halifax area with an L-shaped scheme that twists toward views of Point Pleasant Park and open water, featuring an internal court and multiple viewing zones.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Moore Studio
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A 2500 sqft residential studio designed for empty-nesters to pursue artistic ambitions, built on a tight budget of $150/sq.ft by a young team of builders using crafted construction.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Harbour Heights
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A minimalist cedar-clad residential house with a gable design overlooking Inverness Harbour, featuring a single-storey presentation from the main road and a second storey of glass and cedar cladding on the hillside side, with the main living spaces on the entrance level.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Black Gables
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: Two modest gabled residential buildings with jet black exteriors and metal roofs, positioned at skewed angles to optimize views and daylighting, featuring a private side with expansive glazing overlooking the landscape and seascape, and a public-facing dark façade with minimal glazing for privacy.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Cabot Links Villas
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: Golf villas combining upscale modern amenities with a picturesque shoreline setting that references the origins of golf, completed at 1,300 sqft per unit.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Shantih
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential refuge composed of contrasting identities with two arms wrapping around sloping land toward the sea, described as modest yet elaborate and finely crafted.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: The Lookout at Broad Cove Marsh
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A 2,000 sqft residential house situated on a narrow coastal lot between a tree-lined road and ocean cliff, designed for a Toronto couple as a family retreat with expansive sunset views over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Lady Marmalade
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A renovated restaurant and hospitality space located on Broadview Avenue, designed in collaboration with SvN for a Toronto brunch establishment.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: rchmnd
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A multi-brand fashion retail store located on the ground floor of Historic Granville Block in downtown Halifax, curating established and emergent international designers in a harmonious yet provocative interior space.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Teph Inlet
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A summer home composed of three rectilinear volumes with red cedar-clad horizontal boards on the main house and a glass-encased ground level, featuring massive sliding glass panels opening to a pool and deck, with an adjacent pool house and aluminum panel-clad garage.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Rabbit Snare Gorge
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential cabin built on a steeply-gorged property in Cape Breton with historical significance to the client's family, who had used the land for rabbit snaring and laundry washing.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Brar Residence
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A 3000 sqft residential home designed to accommodate a family with two young daughters and the client's mother, prioritizing multi-generational living and accessibility.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Lake Joseph Cottage
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A gable-form residence on a small island featuring a heavy stone band anchoring the structure to exposed granite, with a peaked wood volume above, using local stone, dark wood siding, and dark metals to blend into the surrounding pine forest environment.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Schlotfeldt Residence
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A corten-clad house situated high above the Okanagan valley within the mountain landscape, designed to resemble a land ship.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Treow Brycg
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A fortress-like residential structure with a canted back shell inspired by local gambrel-roofed barns, situated on Kingsburg Beach and designed to withstand unpredictable Nova Scotian weather.
A reimagined family home situated on a hilltop property north of Lake Ontario, overlooking natural features including a creek, pond, maple grove, and treed woodlot.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Sluice Point
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential house located on a forested high point in southern Nova Scotia with views of marshland, islands, and the Tusket River.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Float
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential home in Halifax's Purcell's Cove inspired by the dramatic glacial landscape of jagged bedrock, overlooking lakes and the ocean.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Peggy's Cove Viewing Platform
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A civic infrastructure improvement project featuring a viewing platform designed with respect for the natural landscape, local character, and accessibility for visitors to the iconic Canadian landmark.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Syncline
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A quiet, masculine modern residential home located in south end Halifax on a geological syncline, overlooking the North-West Arm adjacent to Point Pleasant Park.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Leaf House
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential sanctuary beside a natural spring featuring a curved roof shell inspired by organic leaf forms, expansive windows framing water and forest views, and seamlessly integrated indoor-outdoor spaces.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: The Outlier Hotel
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A boutique luxury hotel in development in the Ozark Mountains, designed to blend contemporary design with the natural landscape.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Art Gallery of Nova Scotia
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A cultural institution of 138,700 square feet designed with Mi'kmaq traditions, stories and meaning at the root of its architectural concept.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: The Blue House
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A community-based housing project for African Nova Scotians facing barriers to housing, designed to support healing and well-being for its residents.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: MODL
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A civic community building with a contemporary and traditional composition featuring a cranked hip roof, buff brick and wood base, locally-sourced materials, and naturally lit spaces with surrounding views.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: OG Exhibition at Beaverbrook Gallery
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: An exhibition showcasing images and models from a decade of the firm's practice, featuring a centrally located enclosure with a competition-winning model of the Art Gallery of Nova Scotia.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Pavilion
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A condo renovation featuring rich stone and warm wood interiors across multiple stories, with carefully controlled natural light that emphasizes the depth of materials.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Riverbend
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A new civic library designed to sit on the land like a glacial erratic, serving as a landmark for the community.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: East River
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential house situated along Nova Scotia's rugged shoreline, conceived for a couple relocating from Montreal seeking a life more deeply rooted in nature and defined by the presence of the Atlantic.

Omar Gandhi Architect.name: Cedar's Kin
Omar Gandhi Architect.description: A residential home nestled into a cedar forest on a steep hillside, organized as interconnected volumes that step down toward the water to engage the landscape at multiple elevations.

Wittman Estes.name: Tsuga Townhomes
Wittman Estes.description: A 3-unit urban infill townhome project featuring a main house and duplex subdivided from a single lot, with Tsuga hemlock wood screens, high gloss casework, and terraced sections that connect to the landscape and wooded greenbelt.

Wittman Estes.name: Yo-Ju Courtyard House
Wittman Estes.description: A single-family residence in the Clyde Hill neighborhood that creates privacy through a series of thresholds from opaque to transparent, blending ancient principles with modern design while adjacent to a busy arterial street.

Wittman Estes.name: Broadway Hill Apartments
Wittman Estes.description: A two-volume apartment building in Capitol Hill featuring a central outdoor garden stairway, backyard reflecting pond, and rooftop patio to provide light and connection to nature in a dense urban site.

Wittman Estes.name: Aldo Beach House
Wittman Estes.description: A transformed 1940s beach house that doubles the livable area for multi-generational use, featuring two shifting wings hovering over the hillside supported by thin steel columns and pin piles while minimizing impact on the waterfront ecology.

Wittman Estes.name: Grasshopper Studio
Wittman Estes.description: A studio and guesthouse for a family with three small children, built primarily of recycled materials, with the main house and studio linked by a covered breezeway that integrates landscape and architecture around a private courtyard.

Wittman Estes.name: Hillside Garden
Wittman Estes.description: A hillside home for an active young couple featuring reconfigured kitchen and dining areas that open to a terrace overlooking Lake Washington, integrated with vibrant new gardens and outdoor living spaces across a steeply sloped lot.

Wittman Estes.name: Queen Anne Garden
Wittman Estes.description: A residential project featuring architectural reconfiguration that blurs transitions between indoor and outdoor spaces, with a reconfigured kitchen and dining area opening to a new terrace overlooking Lake Washington, screened courtyard patios, and landscape design by Jody Estes and Matt Wittman.

Wittman Estes.name: Madison Alpine Garden
Wittman Estes.description: An urban residence with a reconfigured kitchen and dining area opening to a terrace overlooking Lake Washington, featuring a courtyard garden with native bonsai pines and high alpine plantings within a boundary wall with living screen.

Wittman Estes.name: Laurelhurst Courtyard Garden
Wittman Estes.description: A large-scale remodel of a mid-century modern house that opens up living and dining areas to the landscape and Lake Washington views, featuring a central atrium garden with Japanese influences, reflecting pool, and integrated wood and concrete surfaces for indoor-outdoor flow.

Wittman Estes.name: Hood Cliff Retreat
Wittman Estes.description: A family retreat comprising a repurposed 1962 cabin, new addition, and bunkhouse, featuring a material palette of marble, oak, cedar, and terrazzo, with indoor-outdoor kitchen connections and high clerestory windows designed to connect occupants with the Puget Sound ecosystem.

Wittman Estes.name: Capitol Hill Courtyard Garden
Wittman Estes.description: A single-family residence featuring interconnected gardens at multiple levels, including a central courtyard with Stewartia trees, sedum green roofs with Lake Washington views, and landscape elements such as silver vein Parthenocissus vines on concrete walls and basalt pavers through planted beds.

Wittman Estes.name: Mercer Modern
Wittman Estes.description: A mid-century home on a Lake Washington hillside that was remodeled to open the interior to the landscape through new terraces and reconfigured living spaces, featuring materials including marble, oak, cedar, ipe wood, and bronze fixtures.

Wittman Estes.name: Whidbey Puzzle Prefab
Wittman Estes.description: A prefab house that merges high-performance sustainability with customizable, site-responsive design, achieving carbon-negative performance while maintaining craft detail.

Wittman Estes.name: Peach Court Garden ADU
Wittman Estes.description: A modern renovation of a 1910 Seattle Craftsman house with an added garden-level ADU featuring panoramic doors, a sunken garden courtyard, and landscape connections across three levels.

Wittman Estes.name: Everen Wines
Wittman Estes.description: A wine-tasting facility surrounded by vineyards and wheat fields, featuring raked concrete, rough cut stone, and weathered wood that evoke the surrounding landscape.

Wittman Estes.name: Fire Station 67
Wittman Estes.description: A prefabricated modular fire station built from steel cubes and modules, designed for rapid assembly and future repurposing, featuring an open-air apparatus bay and firetruck-red exterior visible from a distance.

Wittman Estes.name: Othello Gardens
Wittman Estes.description: An 11-unit multi-family community featuring bio-filtration planters that channel rainwater from roof terraces through cascading gardens to provide privacy, green space, and wildlife habitat.

Wittman Estes.name: Whidbey Uparati
Wittman Estes.description: A 1,880 square foot meditation retreat with two bedrooms and two bathrooms that floats above a meadow, minimizing its visual and physical impact on the land through a wood-focused design that blends into the site.

Wittman Estes.name: French Creek Workshops
Wittman Estes.description: A new family retreat nestled alongside a wetland featuring a courtyard composed of living spaces and workshops for weaving, glass blowing, and furniture making, with a roof designed to turn rainwater into garden pools.

Wittman Estes.name: Wenatchee River Cabin
Wittman Estes.description: A one-bedroom retreat built of concrete and steel that balances shelter and nature while serving as a basecamp for outdoor adventures in proximity to the Wenatchee River and Okanogan Wenatchee National Forest.

Wittman Estes.name: Walnut Expansion
Wittman Estes.description: A 1908 Seattle Craftsman house expanded with new main and upper-floor extensions featuring modern bay windows and enhanced outdoor space for a family of six.

Wittman Estes.name: Blakely Island Cabin
Wittman Estes.description: A 400 square foot guest cabin suspended on stilts within a forest on the Salish Sea, featuring a small kitchen, murphy bed, bathroom, and loft with bunks, designed in the tradition of minimalist retreats like Walden Cabin.

Wittman Estes.name: The Hideaway
Wittman Estes.description: An art collector's weekend house perched on a rocky outcrop overlooking a remote mountain lake, cantilevering within the trees to balance privacy and expansive views.

Wittman Estes.name: Civic Hotel
Wittman Estes.description: A three-story, 27,433-square-foot boutique hotel originally built in 1962 that was transformed with modern interiors and outdoor spaces blending mid-century design with contemporary technology, featuring 52 refurbished guest rooms, new lobby, meeting space, and gym.

Wittman Estes.name: 4th Avenue Apartments
Wittman Estes.description: A 14-unit two-story apartment community nestled among mature fir trees with terraced site design to minimize parking and maximize connection to nature.

Wittman Estes.name: Madrona House
Wittman Estes.description: A modernized house originally designed by Wendell Lovett, perched on a steep slope overlooking Lake Washington, featuring wood, stainless steel, concrete, and glass materials arranged to create transparency and indoor-outdoor living spaces with terraces and decks.

Wittman Estes.name: Forest House
Wittman Estes.description: A single-story residential renovation featuring interconnected pavilions that follow natural topography and blur the boundary between indoor and outdoor space, with reconfigured kitchen and dining areas opening to a terrace with filtered views of the Cascade Mountains and Lake Washington.

Felipe Assadi.name: Casa H

Felipe Assadi.name: Casa Manns
Felipe Assadi.description: A residential project by Felipe Assadi with collaborators Trinidad Schönthaler, Sebastián Delpino, and Sofía Valdivieso, documented during construction.

Felipe Assadi.description: An 80-square-meter prefabricated modular transportable house with three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and integrated living/dining/kitchen space, constructed from four identical modules with an iron chassis clad in pinewood inside and out.

Tato Architects.name: Paper Tape Shed
Tato Architects.location: Venue design for the BE KOBE MEETING held at KIITO, Design and Creative Center Kobe. Working within a limited budget, we chose paper streamers as the primary material. In the port city of Kobe, when a ship sets sail, paper streamers stretch between the departing passengers and those seeing them off — a material that evokes the city itself. Circular frames holding up the streamers are suspended by a few wires and balloons, keeping the canopies in shape. The title refers to the Paper Tube Shed we once designed together with children at this same venue.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Industrigata Office
STRÅ arkitekter.description: The firm's own office renovation in an early twentieth-century building that preserves traces of previous tenants, including an uncovered painted fish mural, with an open floor plan using a custom semi-circular curtain to create flexible meeting and workspace areas as needed.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Linnekleppen Lookout Tower
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A public lookout tower and fire watch structure combining engineered timber and steel, referencing both the original 1908 timber construction and the 1936 concrete tower with its signature red stairs.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Sauna Furuholmen
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A sauna building in a Finnish archipelago with two contrasting rooms: a dark microcement and granite shower room with indirect lighting, and a sauna room with a full-height window opening onto the water.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Ørje Torg
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An urban masterplan for a town square featuring new interventions including a microbrewery, creative youth club, pizza restaurant, multi-purpose greenhouse, and mixed-use building with apartments and public library.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Vardåsveien
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A residential detail plan for 66 new homes using slab blocks and point houses as noise screens, with protected ground-level shared spaces, underground parking, preserved oak trees, and green infrastructure for rainwater management.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Poolhuset
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A pool house structure featuring two parallel beams running its length that support cantilevered roof joists, creating a pergola for dining, a covered pool area, and an outdoor shower facing the lake.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Knarrvika 2.0
