STRÅ arkitekter.description: A summer house elevated on expressive posts with a two-level volume, featuring asphalt roofing and black-stained cladding, designed to sit lightly on ground between a disused quarry and bedrock.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Hvitstensveien 280
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An industrial park with storage and production facilities for small and mid-sized companies arranged around individual spatial needs, featuring a service building positioned as an active front to the road with generous windows framing surrounding forest views from workspaces and common areas.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Rotnes
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A feasibility study for town densification around Nittedal station proposing a graded density strategy with a new railway park for stormwater management and new crossings to connect the town across the railway.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Glomviklia
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A residential masterplan that preserves the site's green structure and organizes houses in groups connected by forest paths, with shared meadow space and plots facing green space on multiple sides.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Storesand Cabins
STRÅ arkitekter.description: Six identical cabins built on thin steel posts anchored to bedrock, with main volumes oriented along contours and living rooms opening toward the fjord.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Knarrvika 1.0
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A coastal cabin with a concrete base and two stepped volumes clad in Corten steel, featuring deep window reveals facing the Oslo fjord and birch plywood interiors.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Ferry Terminal
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A concept ferry terminal featuring tilting roof modules with solar panels that adjust for optimal angles and allow indirect northern light, with movable sun screens and a modular, prefabricated design inspired by harbor and shipbuilding structures.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Flo
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A floating lodge with a hull wrapped in rough, split spruce trunks and interior walls, ceilings, and built-in furniture of smooth, locally-sourced spruce, featuring a central steel fireplace and wide openings to the lake.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Villa Sandnes
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An inward-facing house organized around a central courtyard with a circular roof opening that tracks the sun, featuring brick external walls and paving, raw concrete ceilings, smooth wooden floors, and perforated timber screens.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Sauna Floating
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A public sauna on Rødenes lake featuring a prefabricated unit clad in timber battens with deep eaves and a pitched roof that glows like a lantern at night, part of a wider waterfront revitalization project.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Villa Fuglenesseter
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A single-family villa composed of two volumes arranged in a courtyard farmyard form alongside a 300-year-old barn, with a glulam wood skeleton, locally sourced pine exterior treated with iron vitriol, and interior plywood wall panels that serve as ornamentation.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Villa Furuholmen
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A single-family villa on an archipelago site composed of small volumes raised on stilts and linked by terraces, designed to minimize disturbance to the exposed cliffs, junipers, and lichen landscape.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Strandhuset
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A guest lodge raised on stilts at the forest edge with a flexible interior plan featuring oak floorboards, solid oak windows, white-painted pine cladding, and a timber wall construction without plastics or adhesives.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: National Log Driving Museum
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An unbuilt museum set into the ground and clad in wood, organized around its relationship with the Glomma river, with public programme and exhibition halls lining the waterside and administration facilities facing inland.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Flishuset
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A community center and museum addition to a transformed sawmill featuring two flexible exhibition and event spaces with timber construction, red-painted gable roof facade, and barn doors that echo the original woodchip house.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Villa Verde
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A two-storey villa on a steep mountainside with an elongated form set along the slope, featuring bedrooms on the enclosed lower floor, living spaces that open above into a winter garden, and materials of untreated timber, grey render, concrete, Douglas fir, and cross-laminated timber.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Bus Terminal
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A public bus terminal with black-oiled timber roof forms that incorporate an open rainwater collection courtyard at its center, designed to make rainwater management part of the experiential landscape.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Villa Bjerkelund
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A two-storey family home in brick, zinc, and metal with oak floors, timber window frames, and a brick fireplace, designed for permanence and to age well through quality materials and careful composition.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Westye Egebergs Gate
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A renovation of early twentieth-century apartment blocks that preserves natural light and expansive volumes while reconfiguring the interior plan with an open kitchen-living zone, sliding panels, and materials of pine, steel, and mirror.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Nordre Gate
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An early twentieth-century apartment in Grünerløkka renovated by its architect owners, featuring a reorganized plan with swapped kitchen and bedroom locations, a flexible dining area with a wheeled kitchen island, and a design palette combining Mediterranean earthy tones with Scandinavian minimalism.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Eidsberg Sparebank
STRÅ arkitekter.description: A 1980s bank building renovation and extension in warm masonry, with reclaimed brick additions designed to harmonize with the original structure's rhythmic facade.

STRÅ arkitekter.name: Vestlandet
STRÅ arkitekter.description: An unbuilt public project combining a biogas plant with educational and recreational facilities that converts fish farm waste into biogas while displaying the production process as an educational narrative.

Surman Weston.name: Hollow Water
Surman Weston.description: A contemporary new build house on a steeply sloping site in rural Devon, with a three-part form clad in copper roofs, granite walls, and waney-edge Douglas fir timber milled from trees felled on site, designed to respond to the landscape's natural contours and local vernacular.

Surman Weston.name: Peckham House
Surman Weston.description: A contemporary infill new build single-family house featuring a monolithic form clad in hit-and-miss brickwork, with a low-carbon high-performance envelope including triple glazing, MVHR, air source heat pump, and photovoltaics, and interior materials including terrazzo, English larch, and experimental lime and gypsum plasters.

Surman Weston.name: Peckham House
Surman Weston.description: A residential project by Surman Weston that won the Manser Medal and AJ House of the Year award in 2024.

Surman Weston.name: Hackney School of Food
Surman Weston.description: A teaching kitchen and community food hub converted from a former caretaker's house, featuring height-adjustable cooking stations and accessible productive gardens designed to serve schools and community groups.

Surman Weston.name: Heathside Poolhouse
Surman Weston.description: A geometric poolhouse in a woodland garden featuring a circular concrete disc platform straddling a level change, a rectangular swimming pool, a timber structure, and a lightweight aluminium roof that extends to create an open pavilion.

Surman Weston.name: Clock Tower House
Surman Weston.description: A six-storey vertical house on a compact urban infill site in central London, featuring a material palette of stone, Portland stone brick, and glazing, with a distinctive double-height glazed clock face, rooftop terrace with panoramic Thames views, and low-carbon structural innovations including calcined clay concrete and air source heat pump.

Surman Weston.name: Surbiton Springs
Surman Weston.description: A 250 sqm contemporary detached house featuring an exposed steel frame with slurried brick infill panels, combining references to mock-Tudor vernacular, industrial warehouses, and modernist design, with a spatial sequence progressing from a triple-height entry hall through compressed circulation to expansive living spaces with timber flooring and exposed steel decks.

Surman Weston.name: Norfolk Broads Visitors' Centre
Surman Weston.description: A thatch-wrapped visitors' centre featuring a 16-metre-high viewing tower, educational facilities, a water-powered lift, and café, with a hollow interior informed by acoustic principles and openings framing local landmarks.

Surman Weston.name: Brunswick Cookery Cottage
Surman Weston.description: A retrofit of a former school caretaker's cottage into a specialist cookery classroom with color-coded exposed structural interventions and services designed to facilitate safe supervision and student learning through experience.

Surman Weston.name: Hackney School of Food Phase 2
Surman Weston.description: A school landscape and learning project featuring growing spaces, play areas, an orchard, and a timber-frame propagation house designed as a replicable kit of parts for educational engagement with food production.

Surman Weston.name: Cork Study
Surman Weston.description: A shared workspace for a musician and seamstress couple in a north London garden, featuring cork bark cladding for weatherproofing and thermal/acoustic insulation, a birch plywood interior with cantilevered furniture, and a wildflower sedum roof.

Surman Weston.name: Makepeace Mansions Apartment
Surman Weston.description: An apartment renovation in a 1920s mock-Tudor mansion block featuring deco-inspired curved motifs throughout, including fluted oak cabinetry with blue timber terrazzo surfaces, a rotating oak-framed stained-glass circular window, a hand-made arched concrete and terracotta fire surround, and custom hand-made tiles with abstracted mock-Tudor patterns.

Surman Weston.name: Writer's Shed
Surman Weston.description: A small outbuilding garden studio with a glowing cedar facade, log store, chimney, north-facing skylight, wood-burning stove with meandering bookcase, and covered verandah, designed as a retreat space for writing and illustration work.

Surman Weston.name: Café Royale
Surman Weston.description: A student union café designed as a warm timber box within a concrete and steel shell, featuring reclaimed materials throughout and playful shutters with festoon lighting.

Surman Weston.name: Lantern Studio
Surman Weston.description: A multifunctional residential studio in South London featuring a garden-facing elevation with a translucent secondary facade, spruce plywood interior walls, and Douglas Fir sliding doors and windows overlooking a mature wooded garden.

Surman Weston.name: Silvertown Studios
Surman Weston.description: A 6,000 sqm mixed-use creative workspace scheme beneath the Silvertown Flyover featuring translucent studio buildings, communal facilities, and circulation spaces designed in three phases to serve artists and creative enterprises.

Surman Weston.name: A Great Tower for London
Surman Weston.location: Wembley Park Drive, London (borough of Brent)

Surman Weston.name: Forest Gate Co-housing
Surman Weston.description: A co-housing scheme combining shared and semi-private facilities including a kitchen, dining room, living room, bookable bathroom, cinema room, workshop, guest bedroom, and rooftop courtyard, with flexible materiality and technology-integrated house management.

Surman Weston.name: Man-Milled-Home
Surman Weston.description: A self-build house prototype combining digital fabrication with traditional self-build techniques, featuring a glulam timber structure, cedar shingle roof, and cork insulation and rainscreen.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Bury Gate Farm
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A new single-family residence replacing a 1950s bungalow, designed as a modern villa within a parkland setting, featuring a two-storey colonnade and constructed with handmade brickwork, rammed concrete, and precast concrete elements.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Monkton
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A new 4-bedroom multigenerational house featuring a rectilinear ground floor plan with three bedroom towers at first floor with mono-pitch roofs, stepped to follow the site slope and provide increasingly generous ceiling heights in living spaces.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Slot House
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A highly crafted 2-storey 1-bed house constructed within a narrow 2.8m wide gap between existing terraces using a lightweight steel frame with fully welded portal frames and handmade pewter glazed tile cladding.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Morlands Farm Dutch Barn
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A conversion of a 1930s agricultural dutch barn into a family home, featuring corrugated metal cladding and sliding metal shutters, with ground floor sleeping and office spaces and an open-plan upper storey with garden views.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: South Street, Lewes
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A four-bedroom house on a brownfield site in the South Downs National Park with an in-situ concrete frame infilled with local ash-glazed brickwork at ground level and CorTen steel cladding above that weathers to ochre, referencing the site's industrial heritage.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Sussex Prairies Tower
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A cylindrical steel tower clad in rolled sheet metal that echoes the form of a grain silo, featuring a helical staircase with circular cut-outs for framed views and a bridge link to an adjacent Dutch Barn.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Flint Farm
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A conversion and redevelopment of redundant farm buildings into two new dwellings using demolition waste and recycled materials to create bespoke graded brick and flint 'bungaroosh' walling as a sustainable reinterpretation of local vernacular.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Bellenden Road
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A small mixed-use development on a former builders' yard comprising a pair of new houses and restaurant extension, constructed from stock brickwork with precast concrete details and perforated metalwork, set on a corner site adjacent to the Holly Grove Conservation Area.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Dangstein Estate
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A substantial new country house with poolhouse and gatehouse featuring bespoke cyclopean masonry walls made from Fittleworth Stone boulders embedded in lime, GGBS, and local stone aggregate, organized around a central courtyard linking to historic estate elements.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Sternhall
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A small 4-unit residential development on a vacant corner plot that reflects the historic building pattern of surrounding terraces while providing access to backland development.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: The Old Cycle Club
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A retrofit conversion of a disused Victorian-era Cycle Club Clubhouse into a courtyard house, retaining original Victorian church fabric and 1970s conversion elements, with living spaces carved from the original hall providing private sanctuary from the street.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Charleston Outdoor Stage
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A temporary performance stage for Charleston museum featuring a sailcloth fabric roof stretched across rafters in bold colors, designed as a welcoming focal point within the historic farmyard.

Sandy Rendel Architects.name: Little Harwood
Sandy Rendel Architects.description: A pair of modest garden outbuildings—a workshop/store and potting shed—with simple rectangular forms in larch cladding and zinc roofs, featuring modular construction with details adapted to their specific uses including covered external workspace and ventilation louvres.

Hugh Strange Architects.name: Architecture Archive
Hugh Strange Architects.description: A private archive building inserted within the remaining walls of an old barn, constructed from a single layer of cross-laminated timber shell with interior fit-out using locally-felled cedar, ash, and beech timber.

Hugh Strange Architects.name: Strange House & Studio
Hugh Strange Architects.description: A small, low-budget house sited in an old pub yard, structured with solid spruce panels and featuring windows, doors, and internal fit-out of FSC tropical hardwood salvaged from Hurricane Felix, with a studio extension added in 2013 using cross-laminated structural timber.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Housestead
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A new countryside house where daily and yearly living functions are broken down into simplified components and expressed as separate buildings.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Contour House
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A contemporary family home organized linearly along a contour, constructed with local stone flowing seamlessly from walls to roof, designed to frame landscape views and embed sustainable design principles.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Secret Garden
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A residential extension with a crank-shaped geometry and sloping double-curved roof covered in brick pavers, featuring a mirrored inner courtyard wall that reflects light and garden views into the house.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: The Narrow House
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A private residence built on a single garage footprint between neighboring properties, featuring a simple internal circulation organized around a laser-cut stair with morse code shipping forecast, designed to display the owners' artwork and sculpture collection.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Pierhead, Swanage
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A new landmark building comprising two elegant pavilions set on a raised podium that creates a large public realm.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Extension, North London
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: An extension and remodelling of a grade 1 listed terraced house in North London.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Extension and remodel, Holland Park, London
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A complete remodelling and extension of a Victorian terraced house located in a west London Conservation Area.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Artists Studio, London
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A transformation of an old jeweller's workshop into a multifunctional live-work space (house, studio, gallery, storehouse and spa) featuring transparency and lightness that integrates professional and domestic needs.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Leamington Road Villas, London W11
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A new house built following the complete demolition of an end-of-terrace house in the Westbourne Grove Conservation area.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Social Eco Housing Emancé
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A low-cost eco housing scheme on the outskirts of Paris, conceived through a limited entry competition.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: The Extension, London
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: An extension to a terraced house that occupies the entire rear garden, transforming the property's verticality while drawing in sunlight and fresh air, with a spare formal aesthetic inspired by the Los Angeles Case Study Houses.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: Swanage Pier
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: A feasibility study for the regeneration of a Grade II listed pier to include a diving centre and seafood cafe.

Sanei + Hopkins Architects.name: National Gallery, Oslo
Sanei + Hopkins Architects.description: An international competition entry for a museum building designed to house three separate museums in one structure, featuring an 'Urban Fiord' concept that provides access from all sides of the city into the building's interior.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Reciprocal House
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A residential extension and coach house replacement in Hampstead that retains and upgrades a 1968 Foster Associates extension, featuring an optimised exposed concrete structure, perforated aluminium sail-like roofs, and highly crafted aluminium interior elements that echo the minimalist material approach of the original.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Oppo Technology & Research Centre Tower
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A 42-storey commercial tower for a Chinese mobile phone manufacturer housing up to 5,000 engineers and support staff, with staggered volumes designed to improve human scale, daylight access, and perimeter views while incorporating spaces for independent work, relaxation, training, and dining.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: The Old Byre
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A conversion of two farm buildings into a home and artist residency, insulated and wrapped in corrugated cement board externally while preserving the interior barn structures, with a translucent polycarbonate facade and spruce plywood interior spaces arranged around a central courtyard.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Casa Kiké
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A private house and writing studio comprising two timber pavilions raised on piles, designed to house a library of 17,000 books, a writing desk, and a grand piano, with glazed ends oriented to catch northerly sea breezes and constructed using locally sourced materials.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Sustainable Low Cost CEB Dwellings
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A prototype dwelling constructed with interlocking compressed earth blocks (CEB) manufactured using 3D-printed moulds, featuring a domed roof, recycled window frames and panes, and exterior render coating, designed as a low-cost, low-skill shelter solution for hot and dry climates.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: House in a Garden
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A new single-family house replacing a 1960s bungalow, featuring a copper-clad pavilion with a complex double-curved glulam timber roof, two underground stories including bedrooms and a swimming pool, and extensive use of light wells and skylights to bring daylight deep into the earth-sheltered design.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Hsinchu Stone Village Masterplan
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A resort hotel and village masterplan featuring a contemporary re-interpretation of a Chinese hill village composed of courtyard buildings of varying scales connected by walkways, bridges, and courts, with landscape integrated as a central ravine spine.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Pink Sand Pavilion & Tower
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A master-planned site project including refurbishment of an existing house, new pavilion structures, a studio and bedroom hovering over the dune, and a guest tower, all constructed from waterproof in-situ concrete with local aggregates and sands matching the pink sand beach.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Light House
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: An 800 m² family house in Notting Hill with an inverted section placing bedrooms on the ground floor and living spaces on the first floor, featuring a completely glazed 'sky facade' roof with variable fritting densities designed as an environmental moderator based on detailed solar and daylight analysis.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Smoking Pavilion
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A pavilion structure built entirely from translucent concrete with PMMA translucent elements and stainless steel reinforcement, designed as the first self-supporting translucent concrete building where the surfaces change in appearance with varying light conditions.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: Palazzo di Riflessione
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A refurbishment of the Piano Nobile of a 14th-century palazzo on the Grand Canal that uncovers historic frescos and timber structure while introducing new architectural insertions in mirror-polished stainless steel and Calacatta marble to function as a family home.

Gianni Botsford Architects.name: The Layered Gallery
Gianni Botsford Architects.description: A private gallery extension for an art collector built in Cor Ten steel, designed as layered spaces including a gallery room, balcony, concealed WC, and outdoor kitchen opening to the garden landscape.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Simple House
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A modest 85m² infill house featuring exposed timber joists, rough brick perimeter walls, exposed aggregate concrete paving, and a central tall airy hall with courtyards on either side, designed on a tight budget to demonstrate that a small house can offer delight.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Lochside House
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: An off-grid, energy-efficient house featuring highly-insulated SIP panels, Scottish larch cladding charred using the shou sugi ban technique, a modular three-volume form with pitched roofs, and sustainable systems for water, sewage, and electrical needs.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Listed Barn House
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A converted listed barn featuring a triple-height central space with two bridges, a bespoke oak and steel staircase, kitchen extension, and two new bedrooms in the roof-space, with timber cladding and panoramic glazing that integrates contemporary elements with historic fabric.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Peterhouse Boathouse
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: An extension and refurbishment of a historic college boathouse featuring new workshop and office space, improved changing facilities, refurbished club rooms, accessibility upgrades with a lift, and a river water-source heat pump, while maintaining the original building's character with sympathetic low-key extensions.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Meadowbank
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A comprehensive sustainable retrofit of an existing 1960s house featuring additional insulation, timber cladding, a wood pellet boiler, mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, solar panels, a two-storey conservatory, and rainwater harvesting.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Railway Apartments
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A brownfield regeneration project comprising four apartments and eight terraced houses with brick and timber façades, featuring shared undercroft parking, street-facing entrances with study rooms, and raised garden terraces shielded from an adjacent railway line by a communal garden.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Elm End
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A contemporary asymmetric house on the North Norfolk Coast clad in cedar boards with three linked volumes, flat roofs with terraces, vertical timber staves providing privacy to windows, and sustainable features including solar panels and mechanical ventilation heat recovery.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Erasmus Building, Queens' College
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A comprehensive refurbishment and decarbonization of Sir Basil Spence's 1960 Modernist building, featuring new triple-glazed windows, wall and roof insulation, air source heat pumps, and accessibility improvements while respecting the original design intent.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Cottage Extension
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A sustainable cottage extension featuring a new kitchen and bedroom with vertical timber cladding, expansive windows, and local materials including Suffolk-grown timber, natural clay plasters, and local stone flooring, designed with low embodied energy and high energy efficiency.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Accessible House
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A new accessible house for a couple and visiting children with live-in carer accommodation, featuring a barn-like character with glulam roof trusses, microcement and cork flooring, wheelchair-accessible design including a lift and hoist runs, and a private west-facing courtyard garden with olive trees and water features.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: The Knoll
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A contemporary extension to a sixteenth-century farmhouse featuring a new kitchen, library with vaulted ceiling overlooking an enlarged pond, and utility spaces, built with custom-manufactured Bourn Great Bricks to match the historic nineteenth-century fabric.

Haysom Ward Miller Architects.name: Stone Cottage
Haysom Ward Miller Architects.description: A retrofit and extension of a 19th century Suffolk farm worker's cottage featuring a new two-storey extension, panoramic south-facing views, solar-panel pergola, traditional flint and brick walls, and decarbonisation improvements to meet modern sustainability targets.

Hudson Architects.name: Coast House
Hudson Architects.description: An award-winning contemporary single-family home in Norfolk featuring a Corten steel-framed main living space with a sedum roof, knapped-flint staggered walls, triple glazing, and Passivhaus technologies including solar panels, battery storage, and an air source heat pump.

Hudson Architects.name: Bavent House
Hudson Architects.description: A coastal family home with a U-shaped plan around a south-facing courtyard, featuring black zinc cladding and weathered Iroko timber, designed to shelter from North Sea winds while capturing views across reed marshes, with ground source heat pump heating and recycled newspaper wall insulation.

Hudson Architects.name: Jersey House
Hudson Architects.description: A contemporary new family home overlooking St Ouen's Bay that replaces a bungalow, featuring a half-level stepped design into the landscape, extensive south-facing glazing for solar gain, solar panels, heat recovery system, and a roof overhang designed for seasonal solar optimization.

Hudson Architects.name: The Eyrie
Hudson Architects.description: A contemporary new family home with a steeped pitch roof providing internal volume, open-plan living spaces, prefabricated timber-frame construction, photovoltaics, ground source heat pump with underfloor heating, and materials informed by local vernacular architecture.

RX Architects.name: Hollington Youth Hub
RX Architects.description: A redevelopment of an existing Victorian community building into a youth hub, featuring new single-storey brick extensions with piers and recessed panels, reinstated high-level openings for natural light, and a new prominent entrance to strengthen the streetscape connection.

RX Architects.name: South Cliff
RX Architects.description: A coastal family home on a steeply sloping site with two floors, featuring off-white brick and red grandis timber cladding, large south-facing glazing with sea views, stepped terraces descending to the beach, and sustainable systems including an air source heat pump and solar array.

RX Architects.name: Sandpiper
RX Architects.description: A development of 12 bespoke dwellings combining natural render, buff bricks, black stained timber cladding, slate and zinc, with open-plan ground floors, air source heat pumps, and a communal nature area integrated into the landscape strategy.

RX Architects.name: Thatched Barn
RX Architects.description: A 15th century Medieval barn, first mentioned in the Domesday Book of 1086, sensitively restored with its original oak frame, water reed thatch roof, lime-repointed Greensand stone plinth, and natural organic insulation with lime plasters and clay paints.

RX Architects.name: Horsmonden Barn
RX Architects.description: A Dutch Barn conversion featuring exposed steel frame and curved corrugated roofing wrapped with thermal insulation, larch timber cladding, and galvanised metal sheets, incorporating renewable energy systems and deep timber-lined entrances.

RX Architects.name: Beach End & Seascape
RX Architects.description: Two new build houses on the beachfront with three floors, open plan living spaces on the top floor maximizing views, three double bedrooms with balconies, built with Petersen Tegl linear white and black bricks, and featuring heat pumps with solar arrays and battery storage achieving EPC A100 rating.

RX Architects.name: Lapwings (The Suttons)
RX Architects.description: A newly built beach house featuring fair-faced concrete structural elements and cedar cladding, designed with ground source heating, solar panels, and high insulation to withstand the coastal environment while maximizing views across the beach to the English Channel.

RX Architects.name: The George
RX Architects.description: A historic coaching inn formed from interlinked listed buildings that underwent complex restoration following a devastating 2019 fire, incorporating salvaged materials, traditional 16th-century roof reconstruction methods, and accessibility improvements through sympathetically designed additions.

RX Architects.name: South Cliff
RX Architects.description: A new beach house with basement and three floors featuring a rooftop terrace, clad in white seamed metal and fair-faced brickwork with polished concrete floors, and equipped with solar array, battery storage, heat pumps, and MVHR systems.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Levens Hall Restaurant
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A contemporary restaurant building with a dynamic roof form, situated on a plinth above the flood zone within the grounds of a grade I listed hall, featuring a material palette connected to neighbouring structures and a manicured hedge running through the building toward the river Kent.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Gosforth Residential Reworking
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A family home renovation featuring an opened-up ground floor with visual connection to the garden, a single-storey extension, master bedroom within the roof void, and underfloor heating throughout the ground floor.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Jesmond House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A semi-detached home renovation featuring a modern single-storey extension with huge sliding doors, chrome-coated fin columns, and a large slit rooflight, connected to the garden through high-quality materials and careful detailing.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Norbord OSB Low Rise High Density Housing
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A housing prototype using Norbord OSB material in interlocking 4.8×4.8m modules achieving 115 units per hectare density, designed for affordable housing using CNC techniques to minimize waste and enable on-site construction by unskilled labor.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Malmo Quay Masterplan
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A mixed-use urban masterplan featuring a cycle hub, restaurant, live/work units, and community space positioned where the Ouseburn meets Newcastle Quayside, with a lightweight structural form for the cycle hub designed as a landmark.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Plinth House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A contemporary house within a Victorian Manor House's sunken walled garden, designed with two main elements (a 'plinth' wrapping the garden and a 'pavilion' above) and integrated off-grid technologies including embedded solar, ground source heat, and battery storage.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Cantilever House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A timber-frame house designed as a new housing model with sleeping accommodation embedded in the lower ground floor and a cantilevered upper block above, using natural stone, timber cladding, and glass as external materials.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Salford Meadows Bridge
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A competition bridge entry spanning the A6 to Peel Park, featuring two corten steel pylons with a deck suspended by cables arranged in a pattern reminiscent of historic industrial looms.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Darras Hall House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A modernized and enlarged dormer bungalow with 5-6 bedrooms, huge windows, and open plan ground floor living that enhances the connection between house and garden while addressing damp and structural issues.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Luanda House
MawsonKerr Architects.location: Luanda, Angola (Dunston Staithes, Gateshead listed as studio location)
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A low-cost vernacular housing concept in Angola constructed from adobe bricks with a lightweight roof for passive cooling, featuring a curved form inspired by traditional African round houses with semi-private and private courtyard spaces.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Calverley Old Hall
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A Grade I listed medieval manor house (13th-17th centuries) on the Heritage at Risk Register, with a concept design proposal to restore historic congregation spaces and add four en-suite bedrooms using CLT while retaining original fabric and creating medieval spaces as livable follies.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Back High Street Mixed Use Scheme
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A mixed-use development comprising a five-bedroom courtyard house with passive house aspirations and rooftop garden, alongside a block with ground-floor office space and two floors of assisted living apartments on a historic alley in the Gosforth conservation area.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Ellison Building Northumbria University
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A university building renovation and redesign project involving a new Vice Chancellor's Office, student catering facilities, and re-oriented lecture theatre with proposed opening of administration facilities and redesigned entrance lobby.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Mill Lodge, Dalton
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A reconfigured contemporary house set into a steep embankment with a semi-subterranean floor for ancillary spaces, using locally sourced stone and slate with modern glazed openings, borehole groundwater heating, and PV panels for energy optimization.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Hadrians Wall Visitor Centre
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A visitor centre at Birdoswald Roman Fort combining refurbishment of existing structures with new contemporary glazed links to provide interpretation displays, café, retail, education space, and accommodation for the World Heritage Site.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Vaux Home of 2030 Housing
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A dense cluster of urban homes around a courtyard designed for the Vaux Housing development, featuring low-carbon construction, flexible floor plates, and integration of indoor-outdoor connections as part of the Home of 2030 competition-winning scheme.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Friar House Apartment Hotel
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A Grade II listed Georgian town house from the 1700s converted into a boutique hotel with 14 suites across five floors, combining retained original proportions and features with modern hotel amenities and 'Manhattan Lofts' style subdivision.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Sacred Heart High School Auditorium
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A renovation and expansion of an existing school auditorium featuring re-raked seating, a new staff and assembly facility beneath, and a dance/theatre teaching space, with natural materials and earthy colors throughout.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Rectory Road Gosforth House Extension
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A contemporary extension to an early twentieth century semi-detached house featuring dark stained timber cladding, large garden-facing openings, and a raised terrace connecting interior and exterior living spaces.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Framwell House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A new office building in Durham City Centre providing 1250sqm of high-quality office space, clad in brick and corrugated panels with exposed steel structure, large light-filled open-plan offices with floor-to-ceiling windows, and eco-friendly parking design.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: CoHuT Newcastle Passivhaus Cohousing
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A cohousing development of 25 houses, flats and duplexes arranged around a communal garden with a common house, designed as certified Passivhaus with low embodied and operational carbon, increased biodiversity, and water management.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Sunbeams Music Centre
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A sustainable music therapy facility featuring passive environmental design with natural ventilation and lighting, ground source heat pump heating, passivhaus-standard U-values, locally sourced sheep wool insulation, and timber construction.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Star & Shadow community cinema
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A volunteer-built community cinema and arts venue in a converted industrial shell featuring cinema, venue space, café, community spaces, artist studios and workshops, designed with a 'buildings within building' approach using recycled materials and found items.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Mount Grace Priory Cafe
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A contemporary cafe building within a 14th-century Carthusian monastery grounds, featuring an oak screen and double-pitched roof form clad in reclaimed local slate, designed to integrate with the landscape and historic site.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Vaux Housing Riverside Sunderland
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A mixed-use housing neighborhood with 91 houses and 41 apartments arranged in five clusters on the River Wear, featuring Modern Methods of Construction, Passivhaus technology, renewable energy systems, and car-free streets designed to achieve carbon neutrality by 2030.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Oak Tree House Passivhaus
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A certified Passivhaus single-family residence featuring a twin timber frame with thick insulation, larch cladding and stone gabions from site bedrock, designed to minimize embodied carbon while providing high ceilings, large windows, and flexible interior spaces across a sloped site.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Castle Eden Crematorium
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A crematorium designed to blend into the surrounding landscape using an earth-covered entrance canopy, local stone and timber, with sunken levels and natural stone walls throughout, featuring internally calm spaces with timber linings and carefully considered natural light and views.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Swallowship House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A single-storey rural house with timber frame and timber cladding, organized into three vaulted volumes, featuring high airtightness, ground source heat pump, photovoltaics, and sustainable low-carbon construction that references the site's former sawmill and tractor shed.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Walmgate Passivhaus Housing York
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A 42-unit Passivhaus housing scheme with timber chassis construction, green communal spaces, and facade treatment inspired by York's historical timber framework, designed to minimize energy consumption and maximize thermal efficiency.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Greenbank House
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A new build ecohouse featuring red brick with vertical coursing detailing, a super-insulated timber frame with ground source heat pumps and solar panels, and ground-floor bedrooms with vaulted first-floor living spaces positioned to capture valley views.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Whitburn Coastal Conservation Centre
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A public conservation centre featuring a lightweight CLT structure with exposed timber panels internally and 100% recycled plastic tiles externally, designed to complement the adjacent Grade 2* listed Souter Lighthouse while serving as a community hub for coastal conservation work.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Grimes Graves Neolithic Mine
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A circular timber pavilion that floats above a 4,500-year-old Neolithic flint mine pit, featuring a sloped ramp for inclusive access, a central glazed oculus, and low-carbon materials including timber and zinc.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: 100 Grey Street Theatre Royal
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A modern café fit-out within a restored heritage building featuring original terrazzo and stone detailing with timber, ceramic, and brass accents, blending historic character with contemporary design.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Auckland Project Glass house
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A contemporary glasshouse inspired by Joseph Paxton's 19th-century Ridge and Furrow design, featuring a distinctive zig-zag roof for optimal light and structural efficiency, serving as the focal point of a restored Walled Garden at Auckland Castle.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Housing Innovation and Construction Skills Academy (HICSA)
MawsonKerr Architects.description: An education facility and training academy featuring a purpose-built workshop 'learning factory' connected to an existing engine shed, designed to be innovative, low-carbon, and net-zero ready while training local people in modern methods of construction.

MawsonKerr Architects.name: Barley Mill
MawsonKerr Architects.description: A sensitive adaptation of a former stone farmstead into a contemporary family home, combining conversion of an existing stone barn with a new living pavilion clad in corrugated metal, featuring restored lime-pointed masonry, retained timber trusses, and integrated sustainability systems including air source heat pump and photovoltaic solar array.

Avignon Architecte.name: Shishiodoshi House
Avignon Architecte.description: A vertical wood-frame house with white PVC membrane cladding designed for a young family of five, featuring an oversized aluminum Japanese shishiodoshi rainwater feature and large cantilevered balconies.

Avignon Architecte.name: 5.6 House
Avignon Architecte.description: A coastal house in Brittany entirely built in concrete and granite, featuring multiple patios and individual bedrooms with en-suite bathrooms opening onto sandy courtyards, with long sun-screens evoking the wooden beach markers of the coastal landscape.

Avignon Architecte.name: (((db))) house
Avignon Architecte.description: A white parallelepiped residence organized around a central swimming pool, featuring scaled cladding on the north facade and extensive glazing on the south, creating a flexible boundary between interior and exterior spaces.

Avignon Architecte.name: Penthouse sur Loire
Avignon Architecte.description: A 6th-floor penthouse organized around a 'vivarium' concept with four distinct glass-enclosed spaces connected by an internal street surfaced in surreal rubber chip bitumen, creating transparency and visual continuity while maintaining spatial separation.

Avignon Architecte.name: Entre-Deux
Avignon Architecte.description: A mixed-use renovation combining a family residence with a contemporary art venue, featuring a central elevated kitchen, thick storage floor, and cross-tent structure integrating bathroom and dressing room with bedrooms and salon at the four corners.

Avignon Architecte.name: house of the choir
Avignon Architecte.description: A single-story house stretching along a narrow lot with a central street and lateral patios, featuring pivoting partition doors for flexible spaces, a pearlescent white exterior with metallic reflections, and an attached shed functioning as a workshop-cellar and garage.

Avignon Architecte.name: down-up house
Avignon Architecte.description: An extension to a ground-floor apartment in a 19th-century building featuring a wood-lined corridor with integrated services, panoramic bedrooms overlooking a garden, and a fully glazed open volume connecting to the exterior landscape.

Avignon Architecte.name: barrettes de chic
Avignon Architecte.description: A townhouse restoration featuring suspended wooden barrettes in a double-height space, a monumental staircase with safety belt straps, white melamine wall panels with custom-made agglomerate moldings, Chesterfield-style upholstering with cast-iron street nails, and fully custom-designed interior elements including a pivoting mirror, spiked bathtub, flexible partitions, and a garden with a shimmering concrete terrace, wood-bark gabion screens, and a black garden cabin.

Avignon Architecte.name: le dernier cubrique
Avignon Architecte.description: A single-story extension of 35 m² designed with lace-like detailing using simple materials in unconventional ways, featuring a hidden patio that connects interior and exterior spaces toward the street, garden, existing house, and sky.

Avignon Architecte.name: patchwork à la flotte
Avignon Architecte.description: A tall residential villa featuring a sculptural wooden interior partition with patchwork wood cladding, containing lofted bedrooms accessible by a massive staircase, overlooking the living space and garden with sea views.

Avignon Architecte.name: All Out House
Avignon Architecte.description: A villa with a 35-meter main facade alternating between glazed, solid, and perforated walls, featuring a thick solar shading element above and interior spaces organized around a central patio that connects to a south-facing garden.

Avignon Architecte.name: atelier C
Avignon Architecte.description: A narrow storage and sewing workshop (2.80m wide by 13.20m long) clad in black rubber grating between two traditional buildings, with colored oilcloth-lined interior walls and a garden-facing window wall.

Avignon Architecte.name: le début des enduits
Avignon Architecte.description: A single-family house elevated to prevent flooding, featuring a simple cubic volumetry with industrial steel framing, double-height interiors with galleries, and infill panels with a patchwork of stucco finishes mimicking neighboring buildings.

Avignon Architecte.name: appartement M
Avignon Architecte.description: A 34 m² mini loft with views of the Baie de La Baule, featuring white-painted wooden slats 7 cm wide (inspired by beach cabins) oriented toward the sea to visually expand the space and define the kitchen, bathroom, bedroom, and storage areas.

Avignon Architecte.name: flip-flat
Avignon Architecte.description: A duplex apartment renovation featuring a high narrow entrance with white plastic paneling, metal staircase with skylight, concrete open-plan living space, and a suspended conical meditation refuge with circular library and trampoline-cloth floor.

Avignon Architecte.name: C'est non choix
Avignon Architecte.description: A semi-buried, minimalist house with smooth self-placing concrete walls and a PVC membrane roof, stripped of ornamentation and architectural details.

Avignon Architecte.name: topless house
Avignon Architecte.description: A 50 m² vacation house addition on the Atlantic coast featuring a removable roof, polished concrete terrace, sliding glass corner doors, and a kitchen counter extending 7 meters toward a bedroom designed as a small house with a pitched roof.

Avignon Architecte.name: Twist House
Avignon Architecte.description: A single-family residence in central Nantes with a sculptural twisted volumetry across 4 levels, featuring a white lacquered horizontal wood cladding, concrete frame structure, and a ribbon-like staircase, designed to respond to the sloped terrain and preserve existing trees.

Avignon Architecte.name: Canclaux Refugio
Avignon Architecte.description: A 55m² apartment renovation on the top floor of a small collective building in central Nantes, featuring open-plan layout with wooden platforms, sloped ceilings attached to the framework, and theatrical curtains to define private and shared spaces.

Avignon Architecte.name: Pagurus Bernhardus
Avignon Architecte.description: A conversion of a former 1960s administrative building into two differentiated residential units, featuring a fully glazed loggia behind the existing facade with mobile shutters and a thermoregulated space, complemented by interior ceiling treatments in custom wood and plaster.

Avignon Architecte.name: Le chant du bois
Avignon Architecte.description: A 182 m² residential renovation for a couple seeking outdoor space, featuring large spruce plywood window frames that blur the boundary between interior and exterior, with sliding doors and hidden rooms throughout.

Avignon Architecte.name: La maison du Coteau
Avignon Architecte.description: A family house clad in wood with specific implementations on all sides, positioned 70 meters above the Loire River, featuring bedrooms designed as camera obscuras with pixelated beveled wooden cube frames and motorized textile blinds.

FMAU.name: Ponte Nuovo
FMAU.description: A mixed-use leisure facility comprising a museum, city archives, shopping center, cinemas, and public swimming pool designed to remediate a polluted site through a bridge-like structure with concrete piles referencing Renaissance engineering principles.

FMAU.name: Maison presque parfaite
FMAU.description: An adaptation of a 1990s family vacation home on Ré Island, proposing the addition of dressing spaces, custom furniture, and interior painting to create buffer zones and improved functionality for multiple generations, though the project was ultimately not realized due to family disagreements over modifications.

FMAU.name: 151 Transformation pavillonnaire
FMAU.description: A construction of 8 student residences featuring cross-through ventilation with natural light in all rooms, a post-and-beam timber structure with timber framing, straw-bale walls insulated with lime-based coating, and linoleum flooring, designed as a low-carbon building.

FMAU.name: 166 Augustoritum 2100
FMAU.description: An urban design study for a 48-hectare neighborhood site in Limoges that proposes to reactivate a historic slope through public spaces designed as miniature forums, commercial spaces, and holistically-planned residential programs inspired by Roman villas.

FMAU.name: 131 Bureaux Sellsy
FMAU.description: An office space layout for a web startup occupying a wing of a former aquarium, featuring custom-fabricated steel and glass partitions with acoustic treatment and dimmable lighting to create a domestic ambiance within the 250 m² open plan.

FMAU.name: 109 Sellsyplex
FMAU.description: An office headquarters for a digital startup with a 5-meter residential grid instead of the standard 2.7-meter commercial grid, organized horizontally around three functional poles (Commercial/Marketing/Development) with shared spaces including a rooftop garden, restaurant, gym, and ground-floor café and exhibition space.

FMAU.name: 010 Parking actif
FMAU.description: A conceptual transformation of a parking lot into a productive space combining energy generation and food cultivation, designed as an idea competition entry for Gaz de France.

FMAU.name: Tropicalisme
FMAU.description: A mixed-use development of 500 residential units and 5000 m² of commercial and tertiary spaces designed as an autonomous building system combining climate control, water and energy management while remaining integrated with the surrounding urban landscape.

FMAU.name: El Polvorin
FMAU.description: A restoration of a 16th-century powder magazine into a temporary exhibition space, featuring 2-meter-thick vaulted walls and ceiling with minimal openings, finished with historically-matched lime render applied using original techniques.

FMAU.name: Esprit Blanc
FMAU.description: Transformation of an 18th-century boarding school into 12 Malraux housing units with new wooden structural framework inserted within preserved facades, featuring non-conventional apartments with diverse spatial configurations.

FMAU.name: Maison bleue
FMAU.description: A primary residence designed with an inverted color hierarchy featuring anthracite gray walls and a light white-blue roof, oriented rigorously North/South with selective window placement for climate control and spatial flow that blurs the boundaries between rooms.

FMAU.name: Escalier du palais
FMAU.description: A corner staircase with steps and risers made of Burgundy oak and plaster, designed to connect two apartments in an 18th-century building, featuring a distinctive landing step cut from a 300-year-old oak tree.

FMAU.name: Grand Caraque
FMAU.description: Renovation of a 1931 Art Deco pastry shop featuring original decorative facade elements, embossed signage, and stucco molded ceilings, with modernized refrigerated display cases while preserving its heritage character.

FMAU.name: Maison Laffitte
FMAU.description: A miniature castle-like residence on a 10,000 square meter plot, featuring a central body with two symmetrical wings housing children's and owner's apartments with reception salons, organized by a 4.40 m module and accompanied by a reflecting pool.

FMAU.name: 121 Maisons à patios
FMAU.description: A development of seven individual houses with patio-based L-shaped floor plans organized as a hamlet-like composition, featuring low-pitched clay tile roofs, cross-ventilated rooms overlooking both street and garden, and modest density designed to integrate with the existing coastal village landscape.

FMAU.name: 122 Immeuble porcelaine
FMAU.description: A 12-unit social housing building that combines modern and traditional urban design principles, wrapped in lime mortar render and featuring 72 repeated 120×160 cm windows in ivory-white, with thin proportions designed to optimize natural light and quiet from the south-facing park.

FMAU.name: 162 Trousse Chemise
FMAU.description: An extension of a family vacation home on Île de Ré that reinterprets local architectural codes with rearranged timber proportions and canal tile roofing at varying slopes, connected to the existing 1970s house by a covered terrace.

FMAU.name: Maison Bond
FMAU.description: A renovation of a historic stone barn converted into a garage for 5 luxury cars, private cinema, spa, fitness room, and guest studio, preserving the original facade while introducing light through a glazed patio and new aluminum doors.

FMAU.name: 095 Panazol
FMAU.description: A design for 34 semi-collective social housing units inspired by traditional U-shaped farm courtyard morphology, addressing suburban residential urbanity while integrating with fragmented existing context.

FMAU.name: 107 Landouge
FMAU.description: A 51-unit social housing building designed with bathrooms positioned as central organizing elements, featuring natural light in all rooms through a narrow 6.5-meter-wide footprint, solid chestnut parquetry, and 2.8-meter ceiling heights.

FMAU.name: Hôtel Miroir
FMAU.description: A mixed-use hotel complex featuring a pentagonal tower with a 5-star hotel, family housing, conference center, and shops on a vast base, with communal facilities including pools and a panoramic restaurant, designed with wind protection and oriented to capture five landscape views.

FMAU.name: 136 Maison cardio
FMAU.description: A vacation house designed to become a family residence for a large sports-oriented family, with 190 m² of living space plus 45 m² of terrace, built in a suburban residential development.

FMAU.name: 145 Fléac
FMAU.description: A mixed-use project combining the rehabilitation of a mid-20th century house with the construction of 8 rental dwellings organized around two buildings that reinterpret the U-shaped figure common in the village, with a soft urban courtyard to the south and countryside access to the north.

FMAU.name: 145 Weiss
FMAU.description: A multi-family housing development of 7 dwellings organized around a communal courtyard with a stepped layout following the site's topography and unified by vegetated roofs, designed with attention to thermal comfort and maintenance durability.

FMAU.name: 172 Petite folie
FMAU.description: A 47 m² outbuilding annexe to an existing house that combines a garage for garden equipment and surfboards, a small workshop, pool motor room, and guest apartment, with a terrace connecting to the garage and overlooking the pool.

FMAU.name: Grange Nouvelle
FMAU.description: A 110 m² single-family house designed to resemble a traditional Corrézian barn, built with stone walls, slate roof, wooden timber framing, and featuring an open interior with alcove bedrooms and a large covered terrace.

FMAU.name: Les Grands Prés
FMAU.description: An urban development strategy project creating 116 individual houses, 6 shops, and 6 offices on a shared collective ground designed to intensify suburban living through proximity and fluid public space.

FMAU.name: 150 Bas Carbone
FMAU.description: A multi-family residential complex of 330 apartments featuring thin timber-frame buildings with natural ventilation and lighting, straw insulation, lime-rendered walls, ground-floor commercial and activity spaces, and arcaded public passages.

FMAU.name: 179 Red line
FMAU.description: A 510 m² carpentry workshop featuring a distinctive red-painted wooden slat facade with angled cladding, industrial shed-inspired roofing (opaque south-facing, glazed north-facing), and six large 6m-high doors opening onto the street to showcase the craft activity within.

FMAU.name: 132 Ciel de Royan
FMAU.description: A transformation of a 1957 building into two family apartments and a gallery, with a mixed concrete frame structure and flexible interior spaces that can function as a large house or two separate units with multiple terraces.

FMAU.name: 165 Logis Gargoulleau
FMAU.description: A transformation of a 17th-century building (formerly Hôtel de France et d'Angleterre) into 11 high-end apartments and a commercial space, with apartments designed as hotel suites featuring generous volumes and enfilade layouts with large double glazed doors.

FMAU.name: Maison Pierre
FMAU.description: A 150 m² new house designed for a stonemason owner, constructed primarily with locally-sourced Paussac Saint-Vivien limestone in standardized modules (120x50x30 cm) assembled without transformation, complemented by solid wood flooring and framing, with concrete used only for foundations and floor.

FMAU.name: 139 Atelier Blanc
FMAU.description: An extension of a carpentry workshop featuring a 6-meter grid structure clad in white corrugated sheet metal with fine waves to resist Atlantic storms, with shutters that open to reveal office windows.

FMAU.name: 103 Maison Beige
FMAU.description: A conversion of a former butcher's laboratory into 2 residential units, featuring a main house with festive ground floor spaces, intimate upper bedrooms, and training/spa facilities, finished in beige tones referencing local stone and parquet.

FMAU.name: Pôle santé du Bois-Plage
FMAU.description: An extension of a multidisciplinary health center that replicates the volumetry of a former convent building while incorporating traditional Bois-Plage materials including two-panel wooden windows, wooden shutters, and red tile roofing, with a restored interior garden and pergola connecting the facility's multiple entrances.

FMAU.name: 171 Garçonnière
FMAU.description: A renovation of an apartment and garage in an ordinary building, where the ground floor garage accommodates multiple functions including parking, kitchen, laundry, and storage while maintaining vehicle access, and the upper floor apartment features two hotel-suite-style bedrooms with multiple balconies overlooking the garden and street.

FMAU.name: La Muse
FMAU.description: A conversion and vertical extension of an existing workshop into office space that deliberately blurs the distinction between domestic and work environments through residential-scaled proportions, a plaster ceiling system with table lamps, and a central steel-framed glass conservatory with a tropical winter garden serving as thermal and hydraulic regulation.

FMAU.name: 148 Bella vita
FMAU.description: A residential house featuring a monolithic blind facade with a transparent polycarbonate garage door that acts as sculptural street presence, opening generously on the garden side with a 10-meter bay window, terraced area supported by concrete columns, and an elevated swimming pool accessible via a monumental staircase.

FMAU.name: Le Roc
FMAU.description: A 131 m² micro-architecture house with stone construction on the ground floor, characterized by a 7.50m bay window with 9 panels, high ceilings (5.35m) in bedrooms, and symmetrical façades, designed to minimize circulation while accommodating a dining area, fireplace, three bedrooms, and pool on a sloped hillside site.

FMAU.name: 118 Maison Taquin
FMAU.description: Renovation and extension of a 1950s house into two residential units and workshops for graphic designers, featuring preserved original marble and terrazzo floors with pale blue tile insertions and exposed utility networks.

FMAU.name: 106 La Bastide
FMAU.description: A renovation and urban improvement study of a 25-hectare social housing estate of 1,356 apartments built in the 1950s-60s, with targeted interventions focused on five localized areas to improve services and public spaces.

Tank Architectes.name: Maison Mouvaux
Tank Architectes.description: A family house nestled at the edge of a wooded site with soft forms and materiality reflecting the surrounding nature, featuring an amplified roof that dominates the design while the ground floor disappears beneath roof overhangs and landscape reflections in faceted surfaces.

Tank Architectes.name: La Minoterie - 44 Lofts
Tank Architectes.description: A conversion of an abandoned mill and industrial building into 44 raw lofts along the Roubaix canal, featuring metal volumes on the roof, exposed concrete structure, and individual outdoor spaces (loggias, balconies, or terraces) with rooftop terraces offering views of the city, canal, and wooded cemetery.

Tank Architectes.name: Médiathèque de la Madeleine
Tank Architectes.description: A public media library in a renovated 1931 building featuring a distinctive tetrahedral birch plywood roof that provides diffuse zenith lighting while protecting collections, with birch wood used throughout the interior and a public garden connecting the neighborhood.

Tank Architectes.name: Carré Janson
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-building urban regeneration project comprising three 18th-century wings of a former priests' hotel, a 1920s archives building, and a 1950s building, redesigned with a central covered plaza that transforms into an auditorium, a suspended exhibition volume, and new concrete circulation towers connecting historic and contemporary spaces.

Tank Architectes.name: Musée des peintres de la Côte d'Opale
Tank Architectes.description: A museum featuring a transparent façade and innovative use of natural light, with concrete 'sails' providing structural support below and wooden 'hulls' joined above in architectural assemblies that evoke the heritage of shipbuilding.

Tank Architectes.name: Le Collège du Plessis-Bouchard
Tank Architectes.description: A secondary school for 600 students featuring sustainable design elements including solar panels for hot water, rainwater recovery systems, and vegetalized terraces for partial water retention, along with dining facilities, sports areas, recreation court, and four staff residences.

Tank Architectes.name: Lycée Léonard de Vinci
Tank Architectes.description: A secondary school organized in three horizontal strata following the site's natural topography, with steel portal frames spaced 1.2 meters apart creating column-free floors and serving as solar shading, inspired by industrial hall volumes.

Tank Architectes.name: Black House
Tank Architectes.description: A sculptural timber-frame house clad in anthracite zinc, organized around a central living space opening onto agricultural landscape with lateral service zones and a cantilevered upper floor with planted terraces, referencing the black-clad agricultural buildings of the region.

Tank Architectes.name: La Halle de Calais
Tank Architectes.description: A modular covered hall on Place d'Armes featuring a long-span lightweight structure with a large accordion door that opens like pleated theater curtains, integrated glass openings, and flexible interior configurations for urban animation.

Tank Architectes.name: Residence Rue Castagnary
Tank Architectes.description: A 248-unit residential building combining student housing, young worker housing, and social housing with 245 studios and collective facilities including a gym and multipurpose hall, designed with an elongated narrow footprint that optimizes interior spaces and employs an alternating filtered facade system.

Tank Architectes.name: 2+2 Houses
Tank Architectes.description: Four gîtes (holiday rentals) of 80 m² each arranged in two bent horizontal branches on pilotis, featuring concrete, glass, and steel construction integrated into a 19th-century park with mature trees.

Tank Architectes.name: Résidence étudiante Eileen Gray
Tank Architectes.description: A 263-unit student residence building on the Saclay plateau featuring varied typologies, ground-floor communal spaces, multiple plots with offset perspectives toward a tree garden, a sheltered common gallery, and dark vertical facades that blend with the surrounding tree line.

Tank Architectes.name: Little House
Tank Architectes.description: A modest single-family house in Arras with a simple wooden frame structure and extensive glazing on three sides, designed to maximize spatial richness and views despite tight budget constraints, situated on a sloped narrow lot with a wooden boardwalk along the south facade.

Tank Architectes.name: Erdre et Parc – 55 Logements
Tank Architectes.description: A 55-unit multi-family residential building in Nantes featuring three levels with private loggias, natural materials including wood cladding in durable pine, concrete construction with underground parking, and flexible interior configurations with double-height spaces designed to integrate nature and landscape views.

Tank Architectes.name: Corten Twig
Tank Architectes.description: A perforated Corten steel footbridge spanning the moat of a historic château, designed as a vegetal metaphor connecting the contemporary access to the restored French garden axis.

Tank Architectes.name: My Little Nation
Tank Architectes.description: A tertiary office building featuring geothermal heating, acoustic insulation, and irregular terraced gardens that increase toward a rooftop, with facades of sand-tinted concrete and Saint-Maximin stone that dialogue with Haussmannian architecture.

Tank Architectes.name: Collège Claude Lévi-Strauss
Tank Architectes.description: A public middle school designed with brick as the sole facade material, organized in three sliding strata without right angles, featuring a suspended helicoidal stairway, a 40-meter sports hall opening onto the plaza, and varying levels of porosity to the public space.

Tank Architectes.name: Groupe scolaire Toni-Morrison
Tank Architectes.description: A school building in a 1970s neighborhood that integrates centennial trees and lush vegetation through organic architecture, constructed primarily of wood with straw insulation on a concrete base and photovoltaic panels on the roof.

Tank Architectes.name: École élémentaire à Montfermeil
Tank Architectes.description: An elementary school designed as a branching structure with four variable-width wings that echo the silhouettes of individual houses, featuring ground-level collective spaces and upper-level classrooms with views onto integrated vegetated pockets.

Tank Architectes.name: Logements à Luxembourg
Tank Architectes.description: An 82-unit collective housing project on the Kirchberg plateau designed as modular, individualized dwellings with varied typologies including duplexes and split-level units, featuring flexible layouts oriented for natural light, views, and exterior spaces.

Tank Architectes.name: Bordeaux-Lac
Tank Architectes.description: A mixed-use development with three distinct buildings containing diverse housing typologies including single-family homes, duplexes, apartments, accessible units for people with disabilities, and a daycare, designed with villa-style volumes referencing regional Girolle architectural heritage and traditional materials that dialogue with the landscape and lakeside setting.

Tank Architectes.name: Maison de l'habitat durable
Tank Architectes.description: A converted industrial brick factory (Halle aux pigeons) in Lille's Wazemmes district transformed into an educational center demonstrating sustainable construction and renovation techniques, featuring an interior covered street with glass roof panels and prefabricated wooden alcoves designed as cross-sectional exhibits.

Tank Architectes.name: Cross House
Tank Architectes.description: A 250 m² single-family house featuring a cross-shaped structural system at its core surrounded by large glazed openings, with black ornamental finishes on common spaces inspired by vegetation and white smooth finishes in private areas, designed to blend into the wooded landscape through reflective and dark facades.

Tank Architectes.name: 89 logements collectifs
Tank Architectes.description: A collective housing development of 89 units featuring larch wood cladding on all facades, chosen for its durability, minimal maintenance requirements, and natural silvering appearance, designed to integrate harmoniously with the natural and urban environment.

Tank Architectes.name: Quartier des Fabriques - Îlot 2B
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-use public building in Marseille housing sports facilities, cultural center, events space, shops and parking, characterized by a prismatic form inspired by ship architecture and industrial halls, with an ETFE membrane envelope.

Tank Architectes.name: Maison DLM
Tank Architectes.description: A compact modernist house featuring overlapping structural volumes on two levels, vertical wooden shingles on exterior walls, mirrored glass openings at the upper level, perforated metal sliding shutters at ground level, wooden deck passerelles connecting to the garden, and a 20cm planted recess around its base that makes the volume appear to float.

Tank Architectes.name: Résidence étudiante à la Cité Universitaire
Extension de la Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (le CNAM)
Tank Architectes.description: An extension of the CNAM research building that creates quality living spaces and a central garden, with flexible compartmental organization allowing interior reconfiguration over time.

Tank Architectes.name: Extension du lycée Valentine Labbé
Tank Architectes.description: An extension to a specialized secondary school featuring a new science hall with full-height glazed facades and curved angles to showcase laboratory activities and provide natural light to teaching spaces and circulation areas.

Tank Architectes.name: Réhabilitation de la Gare de Saint-Omer
Tank Architectes.description: A rehabilitation of a public train station building designed as an eco-digital facility providing services.

Tank Architectes.name: Village des athlètes
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-unit residential and hospitality project comprising 44 reversible housing units and a 126-room hotel designed for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

Tank Architectes.name: La Ruche d'entreprises & le parking Silo de la Tossée
Tank Architectes.description: A combined business incubator and 450-space parking silo featuring a peripheral honeycomb structure that allows future conversion of parking levels to office space, inspired by industrial and textile heritage.

Tank Architectes.name: Centre Nautique
Tank Architectes.description: A sports and nautical center bordering a 45-hectare artificial lake, featuring a 240-meter-long hall with visible wooden structure and lightweight envelope designed to connect the site's two ends.

Tank Architectes.name: Résidence sociale
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-unit social housing residence on a narrow, deep lot featuring diverse dwelling typologies with optimized orientations, terraces extending into existing trees, and varied landscape qualities.

Tank Architectes.name: Concours pour la Médiathèque de Vieux-Condé
Tank Architectes.description: A media library focused on image and performing arts, designed as a stretched rectangular hall inspired by the site's industrial past, with interior and exterior surfaces clad in unpainted Corten steel that will patina over time, and a fully glazed reading room opening onto public space.

Tank Architectes.name: Logements collectifs
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-family residential project on a narrow, deep parcel surrounded by a brick wall, designed to optimize orientation and views while integrating existing trees, with terraces extending into the landscape.

Tank Architectes.name: Groupe Scolaire de Clichy-sous-Bois
Tank Architectes.description: A modular school building featuring green roofs and durable materials that patina over time, designed to create strong connections between interior spaces and the natural environment through oriented views toward gardens.

Tank Architectes.name: Entreprises & Cités
Tank Architectes.description: A conference hall connecting three pre-existing buildings on a 7-hectare park, featuring a dark glass and copper metal facade that unifies the heterogeneous site.

Tank Architectes.name: Collège Maurice Utrillo
Tank Architectes.description: A restructuring and extension of a middle school designed with bioclimatic principles, featuring expanded capacity for 20 divisions, a dining facility, and significantly increased vegetalized surfaces on the roof and courtyard.

Tank Architectes.name: Logements Van Pelt
Tank Architectes.description: A multi-family residential development of six housing entities along a 200-meter site in a former industrial area, featuring four housing typologies with south-east facing terraces overlooking a densely wooded park with acoustic screening berm.

Tank Architectes.name: Pile ou Face
Tank Architectes.description: A house with interior spaces organized along a cross-plan, featuring a glass ground floor, a light-giving patio, a cantilever bedroom terrace, and dark, massive volumes designed to emphasize the void beneath and enhance the sense of levitation.

Tank Architectes.name: Airstream House
Tank Architectes.description: A three-part single-family residence inspired by Airstream caravans and streamline design, organized across split-levels to work with the sloping terrain, featuring aluminum cladding and extensive glazing that frames views of open countryside.

arba.name: Maison dans un champ
arba.description: A 180 m² family house with a wooden shell structure featuring cedar shingle and charred northern pine exterior cladding, birch plywood and local ash interior, heated by a mass stove with passive solar heating and no electrical connection.

arba.name: Maison dans le Pré
arba.description: A small 90 m² wooden-frame house designed for a large family with a budget of €125,000, featuring Douglas pine structure, zinc standing-seam roof, larch and polycarbonate sliding panels, wood fiber insulation, and wood stove heating, where the exposed wooden structure organizes all interior spaces without additional walls or partitions.

arba.name: Le Kiosque
