arba.description: A 110 m² house designed as a sheltered garden pavilion, featuring a natural zinc standing-seam roof with generous overhangs, a wood platform on concrete beams and steel micropiles, local sapwood framing, larch cladding and joinery, hemp brick and earth plaster interior partitions, and wood fiber insulation with wood stove heating.

arba.name: Maison devant la Dune
arba.description: A 66 m² wooden house designed to enjoy the dunes and sea while protected from strong coastal winds, featuring half exterior unheated open-air space and half heated interior, with a black larch wood envelope, wood wool insulation, and wood-burning stove heating.

arba.name: Maison sur le Mur
arba.description: A 132 m² single-family house organized along a preserved street-facing boundary wall, featuring a double-pitched red pigmented zinc roof, larch wood slatted ventilation screens, black pine resin-treated wood cladding, wood fiber insulation, and a common living space designed as an observatory of the surrounding orchards.

arba.name: Maison Traversée
arba.description: A 110 m² house built on a steep slope featuring two stacked boxes in different orientations, constructed with concrete foundations, northern spruce, standing-seam zinc, Douglas pine, and charred spruce, with wood wool insulation and a mass heater.

arba.name: Maison dans la Forêt
arba.description: A 200 m² house in a forest clearing featuring larch cladding and concrete foundations, with layered transparent and opaque elements designed to blur the boundary between interior and forest landscape.

arba.name: Maison dans le Jardin
arba.description: A 130 m² compact house featuring concrete foundations, northern spruce, larch boards, and clear/screened glass, with wood wool insulation and a wood stove, designed to integrate sensitively with an existing garden through low rooflines and modular cladding.

arba.name: Maison dans la Prairie
arba.description: A 78 m² house designed for two people using minimal, basic construction with northern spruce, steel sheeting, and larch cladding, featuring sliding larch-framed windows that open onto prairie views and employing wood heating, solar passive design, and dry toilets.

arba.name: La Halle
arba.description: A family residence designed as a variation on a Norman hall, featuring a concrete basement with northern spruce, larch cladding, slate roof, and wood fiber insulation, combining the main house with office and storage spaces within a monumental four-pitched roof structure.

arba.name: Maison Cosse
arba.description: A 176 m² house designed for an opera singer and family, featuring a larch wood shell envelope enclosing the living spaces across three levels, with wood fiber insulation, wood stove heating, and passive solar orientation toward the south while screening street views.

arba.name: L'Onde
arba.description: A 75 m² house with a distinctive flexible, curved roof (convex on the south side, concave on the north) clad in black pre-patinated zinc standing seam and larch, featuring raw concrete flooring, exposed timber framing, and birch plywood interior elements.

arba.name: Petite Maison
arba.description: A minimal 20 m² residential dwelling with concrete plots, northern spruce, corrugated metal and polycarbonate, larch cladding, and wood-burning heat, designed to maximize connection to an existing garden and sea views through sliding window walls and a sea-facing bay window.

arba.name: Maison près du Sapin
arba.description: A 40 m² small house featuring a protective large roof sheltering a wooden platform, with double-height living space and interior finishes of OSB panels and spruce plywood, using northern spruce, red cedar shingles, larch joinery, and wood fiber insulation with wood stove heating.

arba.name: Maison sur la Montagne
arba.description: A 120 m² chalet-inspired house anchored into existing rock with a minimalist steel structure, featuring larch and polycarbonate sliding frames that open onto valley views, and finished with northern spruce, clay tiles, and wood fiber insulation.

arba.name: La Grange
arba.description: A 228 m² house with a traditional exterior matching village regulations, featuring a bright, open interior with double-height living spaces, wood fiber insulation, geothermal underfloor heating, and materials including concrete slab, northern pine, terracotta tiles, larch cladding, and polished concrete.

arba.name: Maison Relais
arba.description: A 175 m² wood-frame house featuring a sophisticated hollow brick wall system connected to a Canadian well and wood stove for thermal mass and passive heating/cooling, with materials including concrete foundations, northern pine, standing-seam zinc roofing, and larch cladding.

arba.name: Maison Tube
arba.description: A tubular-form single-family house with concrete foundations, northern softwood framing, vegetated roof, and wood wool insulation, featuring a heat pump and radiant floor heating system that deforms with the site's topography to maximize southern solar exposure while minimizing visual impact on neighboring properties.

arba.name: La Lanterne
arba.description: A 45 m² outbuilding situated at the back of a garden, featuring concrete flooring, northern spruce and larch materials, wood fiber insulation, and a wood stove, designed with adjustable screens and a frosted glass patio to function as a lantern at night while providing office and studio spaces.

arba.name: Arba
arba.description: A 108 m² wooden house with pine tar-coated exterior and atrium interior, designed as an intervention behind an opening cut into an existing stone vine wall, with an external covered walkway connecting three gardens oriented to different sun exposures throughout the day.

arba.name: Maison Corse
arba.description: A small 17 m² residential structure designed as a shepherd's cabin with concrete foundations, Corsican pine, slate roofing, and larch cladding, featuring sliding glazed windows and an external walkway that creates a transition between interior and exterior spaces.

arba.name: Arba
arba.description: A seven-story residential building with a curved organic form, constructed with CLT panels, larch wood cladding, and concrete, featuring generously-sized balconies and integrated planted terraces that blur the boundary between interior living spaces and the urban environment.

arba.name: Papillon
arba.description: A 100 m² house featuring polycarbonate and larch wood walls with manually articulated panels that open like butterfly wings to create shaded overhangs and expand the living space into the surrounding landscape.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-family residence built on stilts on a steeply sloped coastal site, designed to preserve the natural landscape and existing pine trees, featuring solid wood construction with bio-sourced insulation and a generous overhanging roof that provides sheltered circulation at tree-canopy level.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-family residence on a steeply sloped coastal site built on stilts with solid wood construction and bio-sourced insulation, designed to preserve the natural landscape and surrounding trees while offering views of the Baie d'Erquy.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Bleue
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A narrow townhouse with a simple carved-out volume featuring a central garden strip for privacy, blue rendered façade with wood-framed windows, and an open-plan interior with living spaces on the upper floor extending to a south-facing terrace.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Noire
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A wooden house with local chestnut wood cladding on a narrow urban lot, designed as a continuous volume with two interior patios to create privacy in a dense neighborhood context.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Jumelles
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: Twin houses on a sensitive coastal site featuring bio-sourced materials including hemp concrete, natural earth plaster, and slate roofs, with ground floor socles and dissociated upper stories designed to integrate into regional architectural character.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Garde-corps banc
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A renovation and transformation of a 100 m² apartment in a historic district into a duplex with open-plan living spaces, featuring original brick structural walls, a suspended kitchen, and an open-slatted bench guardrail, using breathable materials compliant with historic monument standards.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Caméléon
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: An extension of a 1950s house in Rennes that mimics the original architecture's moldings, openings, and facade details while adding a long curved glazed band to provide natural light and sunlight.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Cachée
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A narrow house wedged between two 1930s-era stone and brick houses in Rennes was renovated by preserving its front facade while extending backward with a central patio-garden, maximizing light through large glazed facades on both ends with translucent glass and motorized shading on the south-facing elevation.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Gutenberg
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: An extension to a 1930s stone and red brick house, adding a living space with wooden menuiseries and charpentes that opens via continuous windows to two-sided terraces with generous roof overhangs for solar protection on the south and west sides.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Lostoen
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-story house renovation and extension featuring a slate roof with a distinctive wide overhang (lostoen), dark-colored render, wooden panels painted with agricultural oil to reveal wood grain, and integration into the landscape through reorientation and garden development.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Soulevée
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A 1930s-style house renovation in Rennes that converts an unused basement into a 55 m² garden-level living space with a full-length glazed facade framed by a light concrete portico, while preserving the original stone facade and garden.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Terre
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A seaside vacation house extension in Brittany that creates a twin dwelling connected to the existing pavilion, built primarily with rammed earth (pisé) and wood on a concrete base, designed to provide thermal efficiency while maintaining panoramic views of Cap d'Erquy.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Blanche / Maison sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-story residential home built on stilts on a steeply sloped wooded site, designed to minimize tree removal and preserve natural ground, featuring solid wood, bio-sourced insulation, and slender steel supports with extended roof overhangs serving as both sun and rain protection.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-family residence built on stilts on a steeply sloped coastal site, featuring solid wood construction with biosourced insulation, steel supports, and a generous roof with extended overhangs that preserve the natural landscape and existing pine trees.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A single-family residence built on pilotis on a steeply sloped, forested site near Erquy bay, featuring solid wood construction with biobased insulation, generous roof overhangs, and a design that preserves the natural landscape and existing pine trees.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Canal
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A four-person house on a narrow urban lot featuring a mix of concrete and wood materials, with the structure set back from the street to create a front garden buffer, while the garden-facing side opens generously with a wooden structure and roof overhang for solar protection.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Surélévation
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: An extension and rehabilitation of a 1930s stone and brick house featuring a two-pitched roof addition in perforated brick, interior stone reuse for facade height, and a garden-facing wooden construction with broad overhangs, extensive glazing, and a rooftop terrace.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Maison Malouinière
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A heavy rehabilitation of an 18th-century Malouinière featuring stone walls, redesigned rear façade with new openings, removal of a 1990s veranda extension, reconstruction of boundary walls in the western courtyard, and an entirely replanned staircase, while preserving original interior elements.

Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.name: Sur la pente
Bodenez + Le Gal La Salle.description: A primary residence built on stilts on a steeply sloped, tree-covered site near the Bay of Erquy, featuring solid wood and biosourced insulation, with a lightweight steel structure and generous overhanging roof designed to minimize site disturbance and preserve existing trees.
